text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ year old patient with a history of follicular lymphoma day +64 status-post matched unrelated donor bone marrow transplant who presented with 1 week of paroxysmal shortness of breath. # Shortness of breath: As an outpatient, patient. ___ had a CT chest which was unremarkable. patient had also had an echocardiogram in ___ which showed only mild left ventricular hypertrophy. Given the patient's report of increased pain and erythema of the lower extremities, an ultrasound was performed and was negative for DVT. # Type II Diabetes Mellitus: The patient takes oral hypoglycemics, including metformin. Oral medications were held and patient was covered with sliding scale insulin while hospitalized. patient should not restart metformin until the evening of ___, since patient had IV contrast on the morning of ___. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ with h/o anemia, abdominal pain s/p repair of abdominal hernia x2 presenting with b/l lower abdominal pain x 2 weeks. . # ABDOMINAL PAIN: Initial concern for incarcerated/strangulated hernia in setting of previous abdominal surgeries; however CT abdomen was unrevealing. However, surgery consult found that this was unlikely diagnosis given physical exam. No e/o renal/GU/GYN pathology; pt does have small 4mm renal stone but no colicky pain. Patient had mildly elevated lipase, but low suspicion for pancreatitis as patient's pain was subacute and not severe. Ultimately patient's abdominal pain was attributed to irritable bowel syndrome. Patient's bowel regimen was uptitrated, which was helpful for patient's pain. patient has outpatient follow-up scheduled with patient's gastroenterologist Dr. ___. . # NAUSEA/VOMITING. Zomit was held because not available in formulary. . # ANXIETY: substituted lorazepam for xanax during hospitalization.

text: Brief Hospital Course: In summary, the patient is a ___ old patient with chronic asthma, COPD, NIDDM who presented with chest "tightness" and 3 weeks of progressively worsening dyspnea, worse with exertion. . # Shortness of Breath: The patient's history of worsening air hunger, poor peak flow testing and diffuse wheeze and rhonchi on exam were initially felt to be consistent with a COPD exacerbation. Given patient's clear CXR, lack of fevers and nonproductive cough a pneumonia or infectious source was a very unlikely trigger. Unfortunately, despite frequent nebulizers, oxygen and IV steroids the patient had minimal improvement initially. By hospital day 3, however, patient had a better response. Given the reactive airway disease history one likely trigger which corresponds to patient ___ weeks of progressive symptoms over the last month is the onset of colder weather which can exacerbate patient's underlying asthma . During patient's hospital stay patient described shortness of breath with walking so the team decided to consider cardiac etiologies and a cardiology consult was called. patient had some sinus tachycardia which was attributed to the albuterol nebulizers and anxiety. Otherwise, EKG and telemetry were benign and cardiac enzymes were negative x 3. Total CK had some elevations which may be secondary to statin therapy; MB fraction negative/flat. ECHO (TTE) showed no major valvular abnormalities, an EF of >75%, mildly dilated left atrium, and some symmetric left ventricular hypertrophy, no effusions. The TTE was remarkable for pulmonary hypertension however. patient. ___ OSA and ___ with patient's home CPAP machine are likely contributing to this pulmonary hypertension. . Stress MIBI revealed a new, mild reversible defect of the inferior wall. It is questionable whether this limited defect is related to patient's current symptoms. With exercise stress portion the patient needed to stop secondary to progressive shortness of breath and fatigue with audible expiratory wheezing noted. During exercise, patient had broad anterior chest "burning". This discomfort resolved with rest and was absent by 5 minutes post-exercise. patient had no significant ST segment changes and patient's blood pressure response to exercise was appropriate. Peak exercise heart rate was modestly limited with the patient reaching 82% of patient's age-predicted maximal heart rate. Overall, patient had poor exercise tolerance due to dyspnea. patient had a few of these similar anginal-type symptoms on the medical floor with no ischemic ST segment changes on serial EKGs. patient responded to nitroglycerin and repeated nebulizers well however. Given asthma in all of patient's children and the majority of patient's siblings, an alpha-1-antitrypsin level was ordered but was within normal limits. . You were admitted for an acute asthma excerbation, which likely precipitated this event. We also found that you had sub-segmental pulmonary emboli in your lungs, on both sides. This means that you had small clots that traveled in the arteries that supply your lungs. Combination of smoking and using oral contraceptives increase this risk, especially in the setting of your family history. It is therefore critically important to your health to quit smoking. Our cardiologists helped open up your blockages with special stents, improving blood flow to your heart. During the procedure, your blood pressure became very low; for this reason, we temporarily had to place a special device in your heart ("intra-aortic balloon pump," or "IABP") to keep your pressures up. This was removed within 24 hours. Your pressures returned to normal, and we started you on some new medications to keep your heart healthy after these procedures. Because your heart is not squeezing as well as it should, please eat a low-salt diet.

text: Brief Hospital Course: LEGAL: ___ PSYCHIATRIC: # Mood disorder: Upon admission, Mr. ___ was concerned about paralyzing anxiety attacks and overwhelmed by the connections he could see in his surroundings and the theories he subsequently developed. He described thought disorganization with alternating periods of confusion with clarity and euphoria. He reported sleep variability, including days without sleeping. His mental status exam was significant for mood lability, thought disorganization, increased energy and poor insight. He was immediately started on risperdal for his manic symptoms and hydroxyzine for his anxiety. His insight quickly returned and he became less inhibited and more organized upon interview. At times, he would feel overwhelmed when a theory (i.e. everyone has a reason based on their history for acting the way they act) he developed during the month prior to admission would continue to make sense or if his thoughts had intermittent disorganization, but he was able to recognize these times and use additional risperdal 0.5 mg po BID prn to help with this agitation. Although, risperdal initially caused some sedation, he was able to tolerate risperdal through time and it assisted his chronic insomnia. He revealed the presence of intermittent suicidal ideation during the past month of his illness, but denied ever developing a plan or intention. He reflected with fear on these thoughts. Upon discharge, Mr. ___ has improved sleep and mood stabilization. His thought process is linear and he reports feeling more organized. He is able to tolerate risperdal without adverse effect. He and his father both feel he has returned to his baseline functioning. He has been able to perform his own ADLs during his hospitalization. He is able to recognize the early signs of decompensation and verbalizes his plans to seek assistance, should they recur. He is able to verbalize his coping skills of using art and activity outside to deal with stressors. He has developed a safety plan to reach out to family, treaters or call ___ should his thoughts become more disorganized. Risk assessment: Although Mr. ___ has chronic risk factors for suicidality given his prior suicidal ideation, history of substance abuse, genetic predisposition to bipolar disorder and status as a young caucasian male, it is protective that he has no known suicide attempts. His acute risk has been minimized given his current lack of suicidal ideation, intention and plan, his acceptance of treatment which has improved his thought organization, impulsivity and mood lability, his desire to continue his sobriety upon discharge, his strong familial support and his future orientation with plans to return to his school and work commitments as well as spend time with his girlfriend and meet patient's father. # Substance abuse: Prior to admission, Mr. ___ participated in daily marijuana use and intermittent use of other illicit drugs. He saw a correlation between his use of substances, aside from marijuana, and his symptoms. Throughout his hospital course, he developed more insight into the role of all drugs including marijuana into his presentation. He verbalized fear of a recurring substance induced mood/thought disorder with plans for sobriety. He acknowledged the challenges of sobriety given his social circle, but brainstormed ways of dealing with peer pressure and committed to accessing help through Adcare after discharge. MEDICAL: Mr. ___ is a young healthy man without any medical problems. MILIEU: Mr. ___ was active and pleasant in the milieu. He attended groups, his group participation was insightful and organized. SOCIAL/FAMILY WORK: Mr. ___ views his father ___ as a strong support. His father not only provided collateral, but also presented from ___ to give the patient support. Father assisted team in determining patient's return to baseline of slightly inattentive and scatter brained. summary: You were initially admitted with shortness of breath and a fast heart rate called atrial fibrillation. We increased your dose of metoprolol to control this heart rate. We also found you had increasing fluid around your left lung, which we drained off. We also placed a pleurX catheter to help drain any additional fluid off in the future. Unfortunately, your cancer related pain was difficult to control, and we ultimately found you had broken bones in both of your arms because of your cancer. You had surgery to fix these broken bones in hope to improve your pain symptoms and regain good function in your arms. After discussion with you, your family, and your oncology team, we all decided that going to an inpatient hospice facilty will be the most appropriate place for you to enjoy time with your friends and family.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ year old patient with history of HTN and anxiety disorder who presents from clinic after an episode of chest pain yesterday. #. Chest Pain: patient presented after an episode of chest pain that occurred in an emotional situation and was similar to patient's prior episodes of chest pain. patient was ruled out for MI with cardiac biomarkers. patient's pain was atypical but patient had a recent persantine MIBI that demonstrated a mild partially reversible defect that could represent CAD, although there was soft tissue attenuation on this tests. text: Brief Hospital Course: Pt is a ___ y.o patient who presents s/p flushing, abd pain/n/v, rapid heart rate that is typical of patient's usual systemic mastocytosis flares. . #. Systemic mastocytosis flare: As above, the patient's presenting symptoms of flushing, abdominal pain, tachycardia, nausea, vomiting and itching were consistent with patient's usual mastocytosis anaphylactic flares. The patient was treated with IV benadryl and solumedrol in the ED, with significant symptomatic improvement. Upon arrival to the floor, the patient was asymptomatic. patient was started on patient's home oral medications for mastocytosis control on hospital day 1, and contined on IV solumedrol q8hours for three doses. On the morning of hospital day 2, solumedrol was changed to 50 mg prednisone BID. The patient did not have anaphylactic symptoms throughout patient's hospitalization. The patient was asymptomatic on hospital day 2, and was discharged on a 15 day prednisone taper recommended by the allergy attending Dr. ___. The taper was as follows: 50 mg BID x 3 days, 30 mg BID x 3 day, 40 mg daily x 3 days, 20 mg daily x 3 days, 10 mg daily x 3 days. . #. Tachycardia - The patient was found to have sinus tachycardia with heart rate of 140-160 upon initial presentation in the ED. With IV benadryl and IV solumedrol, HR dropped to 80-100 on presentation to the floor. Tachycardia was likely secondary to vasoactive mediators released during anaphylactic mastocytosis flare. The patient was monitored on telemetry while hospitalized. There were a few brief episodes of sinus tachycardia lasting ~20 minutes, particularly when the patient was anxious prior to scheduled medication administration. . #. Anxiety - The patient was noted to be mildly anxious, particularly close to scheduled medication administration. This was likely secondary to neuropsychiatric effects of mastocytosis, along with anxiety about the discomfort of the flushing and tachycardia associated with flares. Ativan was used as needed every 6 hours with good effect. patient was discharged on PRN ativan to be taken through the duration of patient's scheduled prednisone taper. . #. FEN/GI - The patient tolerated a regular diet without nausea or vomiting.

You were dischared on an oral prednisone taper, and will follow-up with Dr. ___ in allergy clinic early next week. You are being given a prescription for prednisone 10 mg tablets. Your prednisone taper will be as follows: 50 mg (5 tablets) twice daily for 3 days, 30 mg (3 tablets) twice daily for 3 days, 40 mg (4 tablets) once daily for 3 days, 20 mg (2 tablets) once daily for 3 days, and 10 mg (1 tablet) once daily for 3 days. This is a total of a 15 day course.

The kidney stent and kidney drain (nephrostomy) were removed and your kidney function has improved.

ACTIVE ISSUES: # Gram Negative Rod Sepsis: On HD12, patient developed acute onset leukocytosis to 19 and spiked a fever to 103.1. Patient was pancultured and UA revealed a UTI. patient was initially started CTX however patient continued to spike fevers and was broadened to Vancomycin and Zosyn. On HD13, it was found that patient had GNRs in patient's blood. Ciprofloxacin was added. patient continued to have positive blood cultures until ___. patient defervesced on ___ AM and was ultimately narrowed to cefepime. CT Torso was completed and ruled out perinephric abscess. A PICC line placed. Patient ill need 2 weeks of cefepime. Last dose will be ___. # Retroperitoneal Bleed: Patient was admitted initially to surgical service after found to be hypotensive and with Hct of 19. patient was subsequently found to have a large retroperitoneal bleed in the setting of an INR of 2.9 from anticoagulation for known DVT. Patient was given a total of 11 units of pRBCs and 8 units of FFP. Given patient's instability patient was taken emergency to angiography from embolization to stop the bleeding. Patient was observed in the surgical ICU for several days with stable blood counts. patient was then transferred to the general medicine floor for ongoing management. Given recent life threatening bleed, anticoagualtion was not restarted (see below) and IVC filter was placed. # Hypoxia/Tachypnea: Upon transfer to the medical service, patient was noted to be tachypneic and mildly hypoxic to 88-92% on room air. Chest xray revealed pulmonary congestion consistent with hypervolemic state. patient was given one dose of lasix with improvement of oxygen saturations. CTA chest was completed which was equivocal for PE however given recent bleed and improvement of oxygen saturation, anticoagulation was not inititated (see below). patient remained intermittently tachypneic however it seemed related to anxiety given relately normal chest xrays. patient did suffer from a cough which was thought to be related to mild reactive airway disease. patient's symptoms improved with nebulizer treatments. # Tachycardia: Patient developed sinus tachycardia while admitted. Initially it was thought to be related to intravascular depletion given large blood loss and underlying nephrogenic diabetes insipidis (see below). However volume repletion was difficult given hypoxia. PE was also considered given hypoxia and recent DVT. CTA was pursued however was equivocal. TSH was checked and was normal. Psychogenic causes (given history of bipolar disorder) and medication related tachycardia (largely duloxetine) were also considered however after discussion with psychiatry this appeared less likely. Patient ultimately started on metoprolol with good response. # Polyuria/Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus: After aggressive fluid resuscitation and in the setting of underlying nephrogenic diabetes insipidus from chronic lithium use patient developed polyuria (urinating upwards to 13L per day). patient as a resulted developed hypernatremia to 151 and while in the surgical ICU was given D5W. patient was also started on amloride however given hyperkalemia, it was discontinued. While on the medical floor, patient continued to have polyuria. Renal was consulted and recommended increasing access to free water and allowing for autoequilibration. By ___, patient seemed to remain euvolemic without requiring any interventions. # Delirium: On arrival to ___, in the setting of acute illness, patient was delirious. Psychiatry was consulted who suggested using olanzapine BID with prn doses. With resolution of acute illness, delirium improved dramatically. # Recent DVT: Patient was recently diagnosed with DVT and was placed on lovenox and coumadin. It was thought that patient's RP bleed was related to a fall in the setting of being anticoagulated. While patient remained stable and Hct was stable, patient remained a fall risk. Anticoagulation in this setting was deemed a major risk. While patient's CTA chest was equivocal patient clinically improved without anticoagulation. A discussion was had with the patient and husband regarding the risks and benefits of anticoagulation and it was decided to hold on anticoagulation until patient becomes stronger from a mobility standpoint. This will need to be readdressed in a couple of weeks. # Deconditioning: Given extensive hospitalization, patient became deconditioned. Physical therapy saw patient and recommended rehab. It should be noted that the goal of patient. ___ is to ultimately return home once patient is stronger. # Bipolar Disorder: Patient with prior history bipolar and had been on lithium in the past. Recently patient had lithium toxicity and lithium was ultimately stopped. After discussion with ___ psychiatry and outpatient psychiatry, patient was started on olanzapine for mood stabilization. # IV Contrast Filitration: On HD#15, patient underwent CT torso to evaluate for abscess/fluid collection given persistent fevers (see below). While at CT, IV contrast infiltrated skin. Plastics and hand were consulted who felt hand was safe. They recommended hand elevation and frequent exams. On discharge there was no evidence of compartment syndrome or skin necrosis. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: - RP Bleed: Patient's hematocrit has been stable. patient will need follow up CBC on ___ to ensure Hematocrit stability - GNR Bacteremia: Patient will continue cefepime until ___. At this time, ___ line can be discontinued - Tachycardia: Patient should have metoprolol titrated for goal HR < 90. - Anticoagulation: Coumadin held given recent bleed and fall risk however anticoagulation should be readdressed once patient is stronger.

You also required several units of blood to replace the blood your lost. While admitted you developed a urinary tract infection which spread to your blood and made you very sick. We treated you with antibiotics and the bacteria cleared from your blood. Because of the severity of your infection however you will require IV antibiotics for several days. The last day of antibiotics will be on ___. Your heart rate was also elevated while you were admitted and we started you on a medication to slow your heart rate. Because of the bleed that your suffered and because you remain at risk for bleeding, we have decided to hold Coumadin until you become stronger. This will need to be readdressed when you are stronger.

His presentation on history was most consistent with either an anxiety episode, a possible dystonic reaction (movements themselves were not well characterized by patient) or much less likely a seizure. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ year old patient with H/O hypertension diastolic CHF, oropharyngael lymphoma s/p chemo, ILD, hypothyroidism, carotid artery stenosis s/p ___ transferred from ___ for invasive management of a recurrent NSTEMI. patient's cardiac catheterization and deployment of drug-eluting stents in the LAD was complicated by a large hematoma with hemodynamic compromise after deployment of a Perclose vascular closure device in the right femoral artery. Vascular surgery was consulted. patient was transferred to the CCU for closer observation and management and then returned to the floor once stable. # NSTEMI/CAD: No history of CAD previous to recent small NSTEMI in ___, but patient returned to ___ with another NSTEMI with CKMB 45. patient was loaded on clopidogrel at ___ and transferred to ___. Cardiac catheterization on ___ showed that patient's PCW was normal at 10 mm Hg with mild pulmonary hypertension (38/13/24 mm Hg). patient had a left dominant system with serial 50% and 70% proximal and mid LAD lesions with an abnormal pressure wire study (FFR 0.77), resulting in deployment of 2 drug-eluting stents. Procedure was complicated by a large hematoma followed by syncope, tachycardia, and hypotension after deployment of a Perclose vascular closure device in the right femoral artery. Emergent angiography from the left femoral artery showed no evidence of residual arterial bleeding or dissection. patient's hypovolemic shock required initiation of dopamine. Echocardiogram that evening and the following morning showed "small, hypertrophied left ventricle with hyperdynamic systolic function. Systolic aortic valve opening is brief, suggesting low effective forward stroke volume." Both of these findings were more consistent with hypovolemic shock rather than cardiogenic shock. patient was treated with aspirin, clopidogrel, and atorvastatin. Beta blocker deferred given sinus pause/bradycardia post-PCI. Losartan was held in the setting of patient's hypotension and restarted at lower dose upon discharge. # Shock: Patient with hypotensive episode in catheterization laboratory with tachycardia. Patient's HR was elevated to the 120s and bedside echocardiogram showed near collapse of LV with low volume. Hypotension was most likely a result of poor LV filling from rapid heart rate and blood loss, as patient had a large hematoma after Perclose device deployment. Emergent angiography showed no evidence of ongoing right femoral arterial bleeding, dissection or perforation. CHADS 2 score is 3, 5.27% annual risk of stroke. # Hematoma: Patient with 14 point hct drop during this hospitalization, likely due to right femoral arterial bleeding during cardiac catheterization for which patient received 1u PRBCs periprocedure. Hct stable without evidence of active bleeding and no symptoms of anemia upon discharge. # Leukopenia: Downtrending during admission without neutropenia. HIT panel sent at OSH and was negative. Baseline 120s. After catheterization, patient's platelets trended down to ___ and stabilized upon discharge. # Chronic diastolic CHF: Patient on furosemide 20 mg PO daily at home. NT-Pro-BNP 3827. Furosedmie was held during hypotensive episode and restarted upon discharge. # Hypothyroidism: Continued Levothyroxine Sodium 88 mcg PO DAILY. # EtOH use: Drinks 2 glasses wine per day. No signs of withdrawal at ___ or during ___ hospitalization. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ with a PMH of complex regional pain syndrome, history of chronic pancreatitis (unclear etiology), anxiety and other issues, recently discharged from ___ after hospitalization from ___ with abdominal pain of unclear etiology, now re-admitted with same pain, and elevated lipase. Admitted with abdominal and back pain. patient underwent laboratory testing significant for elevated lipase of 885. Labs also showed transiently elevated alkaline phosphatase, however, supplementary testing revealed a normal GGT that suggests no biliary obstruction. Furthermore, MRCP revealed a normal appearing pancreas without evidence of pancreatitis and no bile duct dilatation or cholelithiasis. Lipase can be elevated in a multitude of conditions including gastric motility disorder such as gastroparesis. A gastric emptying study was obtained as recommended by gastroenterology that revealed delayed gastric emptying with 15.8% residual at 4 hours (normal: <10%). This may be reversible if secondary to medication (opiates, for example). Symptoms are somewhat consistent with this diagnosis, however, there is also a neuromuscular quality. We recommended a trial of dietary modification (smaller more frequent meals as explained by nutrition consultation) and trial of reglan with goal to taper to lowest possible dose (or discontinue entirely). Patient was instructed to follow with patient's PCP (within 1 week), gastroenterologist (as scheduled), and pain specialist as soon as possible. The pain specialist should review chronic illness and recent illness as well as medications. If your symptoms continue despite these interventions further investigation into another cause may be appropriate. 5 doses of 2.5 mg morphine solution was prescribed to help patient manage severe breakthrough pain episodes (often occurring at night). Patient should also review warm/flushed feeling and postural tachycardia with pain specialist as we feel this may be an autonomic dysfunction component of CRPS or medication side effect (vs withdrawal). Patient advised to follow with PCP on incidental finding on CXR, reported as "New subcentimeter radiodensities project over the right lung apex and superior and inferior to the distal left clavicle on AP view, which may be external to the patient.". There was concern these abornmalities were external to the patient, but nothing was identified when examined (unclear temporal relationship to study, however). Patient should likely have repeat imaging in a few weeks. Hospital course, assessment, and discharge plans discussed with patient and husband who expressed understanding and agreed with discharge.

Pt had been to several hospitals for patient's chest pain and was diagnosed with recurrent pericarditis. Upon discussion with pt's Gastroenterologist and PCP, they did not feel as if patient's chest pain was pericarditis and were concerned that it may be extraintestinal manifestations of IBD specifically crohns given patient's previous positive IBD serology tests. EKG on admission did not show any signs of pericarditis, GI consult was obtained per pt's PCP's recommendation. Pt underwent an EGD and Colonoscopy which showed no evidence of IBD, CT abd/pelvis showed on evidence of IBD within the small intestines. ESR and CRPs were also sent which were normal, upon history pt also did not exhibit any clinical signs of IBD. Other considerations for the possible cause of atypical chest pain per pt's PCP included autoimmune disease and infectious disease. Both services were consulted, per Rheumatology they did not feel this process was autoimmune in nature. They also recommended sending out ___ which was negative. ID recommended HIV test, strongyloides, toxocara given the pt's exposure history all tests were again negative. During the hospitalization pt's pain was controlled with initially IV narcotics; as pt appeared to be very sleepy after IV pain medication and requested more IV pain medication despite seeming sleepy patient was transitioned to a longer acting PO regimen which will be tapered off as an outpt. Given patient's negative ID, GI and Rheum work-up and improved pain control with PO regimen pt was discharged with close follow up with ID, Rheum, GI, PCP and ___. Although no clear mechanism for patient's chest pain was noted patient's symptomology closely resembled that of recurrent pericarditis which does not always show EKG changes. ##. Transaminitis: Pt was also noted to have transaminitis to the 300s per OSH reports. Differential included infectious disease, medications. Viral hepatitis was ruled out on serology testing at OSH. Viral infection could also include a mild rise in transaminases. During patient's hospitalization patient's LFTs were trended and were noted to decrease. Medications were also considered given a conversation with the pt and patient's family. Pt was prescribed Percocet for patient's chest pain but endorsed only taking several pills a week. Pt's father was at patient's bedside and stated patient had taken a lot more Percocet, per him patient had gone through 40-50 pills over the past few weeks. Pt continued to deny taking that many pain medications. Again unclear as to the etiology, Acetaminophen level was negative however it is possible that this was due to Acetaminophen or a possible viral infection. ##. Pain Control: On admission pt stated patient had ___ chest pain, worse with leaning forward. patient was initially given IV pain medication and then during hospitalization patient was transitioned to a longer acting PO regimen. patient was instructed at time of discharge that the pain medication would not be long term and would be tapered off by patient's PCP. ##. Anxiety: During hospitalization pt was very anxious, prior to patient's discharge pt stated that patient didnt feel ready for discharge despite patient's pain being well controlled objectively on patient's PO regimen. The patient was evaluated by infectious disease and started on ganciclovir. patient will continue IV induction therapy via ___ through ___, will follow up with ID and OPAT to determine course of valganciclovir after completion of IV induction. text: Brief Hospital Course: # Pneumonia: The patient was admitted to the medicine service for new left upper lobe pneumonia thought to be consistent with aspiration. patient was started on vancomycin and meropenem. Given patient was afebrile, no leukocytosis and was hemodynamically stable vancomycin was discontinued two days into admission meropenem was continued for a 10 day course. On day 10 of admission patient was found to be somnolent in the morning. Per patient's daughter patient received valerian root overnight for insomnia and anxiety. ABG indicated respiratory acidosis, with PCO2 at 81 (baseline high ___ to 60). patient was transferred to the ICU for further management. patient was started on BiPAP until patient's blood gas improved. patient was able to come off to eat patient's dinner. patient was put back on BiPAP overnight to get some rest. In the morning, patient again came off and continued to do well. Patient did receive one 250cc bolus for hypotension and an appropriate increase in patient's blood pressure. patient completed patient 10 days of meropenem. Prior to discharge patient was scheduled for a sleep study to further evaluate for home bipap. . # Diastolic Heart Failure: Echo done on previous discharge showed mild LVH, hyperdynamic systolic function (EF>75%), right ventricular pressure/volume overload, 2+TR, and moderate pulmonary artery hypertension. patient's lasix was continued at 10mg daily and intake/output was monitored as well. patient continued to do well without need for further intervention. Prior to discharge patient was restarted on patient's home beta blocker (metoprolol succinate 12.5mg PO bid) with good BP control. . # CKD: Admitted with Cr of 2.3, which was near patient's baseline. With conservative treatment creatinine improved to 1.4. Nephrotoxins were avoided. . # Crohn's Disease: patient did not experience frequent bouts of diarrhea on this admission. Prednisone taper was initially continued, but changed to a slower taper per daughters request. Ciprofloxacin and mesalamine was continued. . # MDS and Related Anemia: patient was given 1U PRBC for hct 24, and weekly epogen was restarted on this admission. patient will need further follow-up with hematology. . # DVT/PE: Patient had chronic DVT/PE in the past for which patient was on lovenox. The patient's daughter refused heparin (previous history of worsening thrombocytopenia w/use although HIT Ab negative) and pneumoboot to arm given patients poor skin condition. summary: You were admitted to the hospital for a TACE (transarterial chemoembolization) for liver metastases. This procedure was complicated by some of the TACE/chemotherapy going to the lung and causing a low oxygen level. This was treated with oxygen support, steroids (to decrease inflammation), diuretics (to remove excess fluid on the lungs), and transfer to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU). The steroids, to treat the inflammation in your lungs, caused mood changes and confusion so they were stopped. As can be expected, the TACE procedure was also complicated by hepatic encephalopathy (confusion due to the liver) and abnormal liver function tests. You will need physical therapy at rehabilitation to regain your strength and balance.

text: Brief Hospital Course: BRIEF HISTORY: The patient is a ___ w/ HBV, HCV, substance abuse disorder with active intravenous drug use, presenting w/ 3 weeks of back pain. On presentation, a CT scan and MRI of the lumbar spine demonstrated a large epidural abscess compressing the cauda equina nerve roots, with associated L5/S1 discitis/osteomyelitis. The patient was started on IV vancomycin and cefepime for broad spectrum coverage, and treated with IV dilaudid for pain control. patient underwent an anterior and posterior approach epidural abscess drainage and L5-S1 vertebral body washout with the installation of hardware for structural support. Cultures were drawn intraoperatively which grew Staph Aureus, matching the blood cultures from the OSH. With this data, cefepime was discontinued, and the patient was continued on Vancomycin for coverage of both MSSA and MRSA. The cultures eventually spectated to MRSA and the patient was continued on vancomycin. For pain control post operatively, the acute pain service was consulted who managed a ketamine drip for 48 hours. In addition, the pt was given a Dilaudid PCA, Acetaminophen 1000mg, and Gabapentin 600mg. When the pain was better controlled, the patient was started on an oral regimen, with IV dilaudid PRN. The patient also developed an acute on chronic anemia, with a hemoglobin of 6.4, for which patient was transfused one unit of pRBCs. The patient continued to have pain control issues and was maintain on IV and PO dilaudid. On ___, the patient continued to spike fevers. A CT abdomen/ pelvis was done, which showed a new 4 cm fluid collection with peripheral enhancement and stranding medial to the bifurcation of the left common iliac artery, worrisome for infection. On ___, ___ placed drains in and drained a superior, inferior, and abdominal collection. The patient then had resolution of patient's fevers, but worsening pain. Chronic pain was consulted and patient's regimen was changed to Morphine ___ 15mg q4h and patient's none opioid medications were optimized. Patient was seen by social work for discussion of long term treatment plans of Opioid Use disorder. The patient preferred suboxone and on ___ patient's opioids and diazepam were stopped. On ___ when the patient's ___ was 8, the patient received one 4mg dose of suboxone around noon. Soon after patient became anxious and stated patient wanted to leave AMA. Infectious disease, the ___ medicine attending, and social work spoke to the patient extensively about the risks of leaving AMA, including the danger of leaving with an incomplete treatment of discitis/osteomyelitis, particularly in the setting of having hardware in place. Patient still decided to leave AMA after hearing all the risks of leaving, including death and worsening infections. Patient was redosed on patient's suboxone to 10mg total. patient watched a video and was counseled on clean injection techniques and Naloxone use. patient's PICC line was pulled and patient was given a script for one month of Rifampin 300mg BID, bactrim DS 2 tabs BID, and naloxone and told to come for ID follow-up. Thought to be multifactorial, including nutritional and secondary to inflammation. #) Opiate use disorder: The patient was seen by the addiction specialist several times throughout the hospital stay who recommended continuously assessed the patient's readiness to start long term OUD treatment. Patient preferred suboxone to methadone, though had previously tried both and relapsed. The patient was nervous to start treatment, but stated "it has to get hard before it gets easier." You were treated for cellulitis in the emergency department but on further evaluation it was discovered that you had a noninfectious condition called venous stasis dermatitis which is caused by swelling. It was thought that your pain was caused by a combination of nerve pain (neuropathy), arthritis, and swelling (venous stasis).

text: Brief Hospital Course: Summary: ___ male with past medical history of compensated alcoholic cirrhosis completed by hepatic encephalopathy and portal hypertension, bipolar disorder, anxiety, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and chronic back pain who presents with intermittent confusion and exertional dyspnea. He was admitted to the Hepatology service and treated for the issues below. ACUTE ISSUES: ============= # Bilateral pulmonary emboli # Bilateral deep vein thromboses Patient presented with a subacute onset of exertional dyspnea that improved with rest. His EKG was notable for T-wave inversions in the inferior septal territory without any elevation in troponins. BNP was elevated to 1276. A TTE was significant for "There is mild regional left ventricular systolic dysfunction with hypokinesis of the basal half of the inferior wall. The remaining segments contract normally (LVEF = 50 %). Tissue Doppler imaging suggests a normal left ventricular filling pressure (PCWP<12mmHg). Right ventricular chamber size is normal with mild global free wall hypokinesis. There is abnormal septal motion/position. The ascending aorta is mildly dilated." Cardiology was consulted who recommending doing a CT chest to evaluate for pulmonary emboli which showed "Extensive pulmonary emboli extending from near right main pulmonary artery to segmental level in the right middle lobe and 2 subsegmental level in the right lower lobe and from lobar to subsegmental level in left upper and lower lobes. No evidence of right heart strain." He was started on a heparin gtt with bridge to warfarin. Due to his known hygroma, a CT head was done which showed no acute bleed. Due to possible concern for coronary artery disease, he was started on prophylaxis with atorvastatin 40 mg p.o. daily and aspirin 81 mg p.o. daily. He will follow up with Cardiology for stress test in ___ months. # Toxic metabolic encephalopathy Patient presented with subacute onset of worsening disorientation and memory loss on top of chronic memory loss. He denies any traumatic event. He had no acute neurologic abnormalities concerning for an intracranial bleed or encephalitis. He had no obvious electrolyte abnormalities and his liver disease appears well compensated. CT head without contrast in the emergency department was negative for any acute process but did show unchanged small left subdural hygroma or chronic hematoma with mild rightward shift of midline structures. B12, TSH, RPR, and toxicology screens were all unremarkable. Notably his lithium level was mildly elevated. Infectious workup was done which was negative for any urinary tract infection, pulmonary infection, or bacteremia. Patient was noted to have mild acute kidney injury, which may have been contributing. He was continued on his home rifaximin and lactulose to avoid hepatic encephalopathy. Psychiatry was consulted, who recommended down titrating his benzodiazepines and opiates. They also recommended stopping marijuana use, as he was reportedly using medical marijuana twice per day for his chronic pain. Occupational therapy was consulted for neurocognitive testing, who thought he had returned to his baseline and can safely return home with assistance from his wife and doing his activities of daily living. He should be referred for outpatient neurocognitive testing. # Acute kidney injury Patient noted to have a creatinine of 1.3 on admission from his baseline creatinine of 1.0-1.2 previously. He is continued on his home propranolol which he takes for essential tremor, lactose, and rifaximin. On transfer from OSH, EF was ___ with 3+ MR. ___ day after transfer showed EF ___, LV hypokinesis, and 3+ MR. ___ was ruled out for acute MI at OSH and has had multiple normal caths in the past. patient always experiences shortness of breath in the middle of the night, thought to be subjective because patient's O2 sats remain stable with no increased work of breathing. patient was initially satting 100% on 4L on transfer and was successfully weaned to room air upon discharge. patient is able to walk down the hallway with ___. Ambulatory sats on 2 days prior to discharge were 87% on room air, however they subsequently improved to low ___ on discharge. On percussion, patient has decreased resonance in right lung base, thought to represent an effusion, but only small effusion seen on CXR and no large pocket of fluid to tap on ultrasound. Per Dr. ___ further optimization available to resynchronize ventricles to optimize cardiac output. ___ was diuresed with a lasix gtt for three days. patient was then transitioned to PO torsemide for diuresis which was uptitrated to 40 mg po prior to discharge. patient was started on losartan for afterload reduction and spironolactone for mortality benefit. patient's carvedilol was increased to 6.25mg daily and patient was continued on home dose of digoxin. patient was advised on a low salt diet and fluid restriction 1500cc/day. Given the brief period of hypoxia during intubation at the OSH, targeted temperature control at 36 C using the Arctic Sun was initiated for 24 hours. When discontinued, ___ remained normothermic. # Hypotension: Pt was hypotensive to ___ systolic upon arrival to MICU and throughout patient's early hospitalization. patient was given levophed for BP support until HD #10. Continued to have low BPs (80s/40s) with peritoneal dialysis but was asymptomatic. Lactate trend: 3.5 -> 3.8 -> 4.0-> 2.9->1.0. Did not give epo; did speak with ___ home nephrologist Dr. ___, about this problem who will follow as outpatient. # Acute encephalopathy: ___ was not responsive to commands until HD #2 felt to be from possible ___ day old hemorrhage vs sepsis vs toxic metabolic vs loading dose vecuronium with no HD vs anoxia. Old stroke with new hyperdensities on CT. Initially exam: pupils reactive, no cornea, no gag reflex. Significant improvement on ___ ___wake, responding to commands. Neurosurgery and Neurology following. MRA vs CTA for further evaluation if deemed necessary (now less likely). Regained baseline neurologic function. Per ___, no memory of early ___ hospitalization; patient comfortable and not in emotional distress during current hospitalization. Did require Ativan and Benadryl to sleep / aid in anxiety during hospitalization, which improved. Was restarted on home psychiatric medications (sertraline and amitriptyline) on HD #12. Neurology and neurosurgery signed off and do not require follow up as patient reportedly back to baseline. #Pain control: Upon opening eyes on ___, patient endorsed pain in throat from intubation. Required Dilaudid Q3hrs to control the pain. There was concern for possible neck/ laryngeal injury in setting of reported traumatic intubation during transport from OSh, thus CT neck was obtained. This did not show any abscess or tissue injury. Pain self-resolved after ___ was extubated. # Widened mediastinum and question cavitary lesions on CXR: Mediastinal lymphadenopathy was noted on chest imaging (CXR). There was initial concern for acute process contributing to respiratory failure, however records of CT Chest in ___ confirmed that these nodes had been previously observed-- it was felt that likely chronic steroid use as a child and young adult was responsible. (NO known TB risk factors or symptoms of malignancy warranting further work up). # Hypothyroidism Continued home 100mcg levothyroxine while in house. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ wih metastatic NSCLC to brain who presents with right sided weakness. # Right sided weakness: Patient does have ___ strength on right compared to left. MRI brain with decreased size of known left frontal mass but increased swelling and midline shift, possibly from cyberknife. The patient was started on dexamethasone 4mg Q6h, placed on frequent neuro checks and was evaluated by heme/onc, neurosurgery and radiation oncology. There was initially some debate as to whether the edema was due to interval increase in mass size vs. radiation necrosis. Ultimately, it was determined to be more likely related to radiation necrosis and neurosurgery recommended resection. summary: You were admitted to ___ because you were short of breath and were found to have fluid in your lungs. The fluid was not infected and did not show signs of cancer. Additionally, you were very tired when you first arrived, and your red blood cells were low. Therefore, we gave you 1 unit of blood which helped increased your red blood cell count. Lastly, you were found to have a urinary tract infection. We treated you with an antibiotic for 5 days. When you leave the hospital, you will still need to use the oxygen because there is still some fluid in your lungs. We have started you on a medication called Torsemide, which will need to take once a day to help keep fluid off of your body. This medication is a diuretic. Please do not drink more than 2 liters a day and adhere to a low sodium (2grams/day) diet. It is also important that you weight yourself every morning.

summary: You came to the hospital after swallowing a large piece of steak. You had a procedure called an upper endoscopy or EGD (esophagogastroduodenoscopy) where a camera is placed down your feeding tube (esophagus). We saw a large portion of impacted food. During this procedure you stopped being able to breath on your own. You had an endotracheal tube placed down your throat (intubation) and you were placed on a ventilator to help you breathe. Your EGD was resumed and our gastroenterologists were able to dislodge the impacted food from your esophagus. After the procedure you were found to have partial collapse of the lower lobe of your left lung. This may have contributed to your difficulty breathing during the procedure. While intubated our interventional pulmonologists took a look with a bronchoscope in your airways and helped re-inflate your lung. You were soon extubated and breathed well on your own.

text: Brief Hospital Course: A/P ___ in good health with syncopal episode during exertion. . #) Syncope: The patient experienced a syncopal event during exertion. Given this patient's age, rapid recovery, and the exertional component associated with the syncope, a cardiac etiology, whether an arrythmia or a structural defect was of highest concern. The patient's EKG has t wave inversions in V1-V3 and right axis deviation, as well as a pronounced sinus arrhythmia. patient had an echocardiogram which showed no structural defects. Cardiology was consulted and also recommended EKG stress test, which was normal as well. EP reviewed the ekg and felt it likely a normal variant given patient's young age and atheticism. Therefore it was felt that patient had no evidence for any life-threatening arrhythmias or structural defects. patient was given a holter monitor as an outpt and will be followed up by cardiology in a few weeks. . A neurologic component was also considered as this patient has many relative risk factors for seizure: wellbutrin use, poor sleep for several days, recent cessation of clonazepam. However, given the lack of a post-ictal period and the nature of the event this is less likely. Autonomic instability including vasovagal origin is also possible but again less likely given this story and lack of prodrome. Metabolic origins are unlikely; glucose was normal in ED, HCG negative, Tox negative. HCT normal. . Given these normal tests, it seems likely that this syncopal event could have been a result of multifactorial causes: sleep deprivation, fatigue during practice, anxiety, recent increase in wellbutrin (which can cause bradyarrhythmias) and recent cessation of clonazepam. In consultation with the pt's therapist it was decided to taper patient's wellbutrin, 150mg xl x4 days and then stop it. patient will continue taking clonazepam 1mg qhs prn insomnia. For the next few wks until the pt's f/u with cardiology it was recommended that patient limited patient's exercise to light conditioning such as walking and jogging. No competitive play. Both patient's coach and patient's therapist were notified of these restrictions, with the patient's permission. . #) Anxiety: Wellbutrin taper started, 150mg xl daily x4 days, and then stop it. Treatment was continued with loratadine and a prednisone taper which patient will complete over 5 days. Aspirin was added to patient's allergy list and patient was advised to stop taking the baby aspirin. Of note, patient is also on lisinopril which can cause angioedema, however given the history the daughter provided and the timing of the medications (patient had taken lisinopril early in the morning, whereas the aspirin was a couple of hours prior to arrival on the floor) made it much more likely that aspirin and not lisinopril caused patient's reaction. # "Chest throbbing": The patient's chest throbbing description was very atypical for cardiac chest pain. The pain was not related to exertion, did not radiate, and had no associated symptoms. patient's EKG was unchanged and patient had a nuclear stress in ___ which showed non-specific EKG changes with no anginal sx and a normal perfusion study. patient was ruled out for MI with 3 sets of negative cardiac enzymes and monitored on telemetry. The chest throbbing was most likely related to anxiety and stress related to relational issues within patient's family. The chest throbbing completely resolved during the hospitalization and the patient did think that it was related to patient's stress. # Hyperlipidemia: patient was continued on patient's home statin. # Hypertension: patient was continued on chlorthalidone 12.5 mg daily and lisinopril 40 mg daily. # COPD: Stable. patient was continued on advair 250 mg-50 mcg inh bid, albuterol 2 puffs q4 hr prn, fluticasone 50 mcg ___ sprays daily, and montelukast 10 mg daily. # Osteopenia: The patient was contineud on Ca/VitD. # Code: full code, confirmed with the patient # Communication: Patient and patient's Daughter ___ ___ ___

You were monitored on telemetry and blood tests showed no involvement of your heart. In the emergency room you were given a full-dose aspirin and you had a reaction called agioedema (swelling of the throat). You were treated with multiple medications with improvement in your symptoms. You will need to complete a 5 day course of a prednisone taper.

GJ-Tube: Patient pulled GJ-tube out during admission. ___ temporarily put in a foley until able to replace GJ-tube on ___. Two days later the patient had low grade fever, elevated WBC and rebound tenderness and a CT Abd & Pelvis showed GJ tube in place without free air, no acute process found. Fever, white count, and symptoms improved. Due to erythema surrounding tube site, patient was discharged on a short course of clindaymcin. . Chest pain: patient was ruled out for MI by unchanged EKG and flat serial Troponins. . Tachycardia/palpitations: Pt had sinus tachycardia likely secondary to pain/agitation. patient is being followed by outpatient cardiology and has a holter monitor on. . DM1: Pt is a type 1 diabetic with poor glucose control. Pt's finger sticks ran high patient's entire admission but we were afraid to titrate up patient's insulin since patient's eating habits are unpredictable. ___ was consulted and helped to adjust patient's ISS. Glucose control was complicated by patient's intermittent refusal to get finger sticks and insulin. Discharged on Lantus 60 units QHS and new sliding scale provided by ___. . Chronic pain/pancreatitis: stable with LFTs near baseline. patient's pain was treated with IV Dilaudid per usual regimen. Given patient would escalate at times with requests for extra narcotics, we would allow patient's one extra dose of dilaudid per day max, which patient would decide when to take (periproceudre for example). This allowed patient's to maintain some control over patient's regimen without escalating patient's doeses of narcotics overall and with fewer behavioral issues. patient was also maintained on po Valium as needed for anxiety. patient was eating at discharge and was not using patient's tube for feeds.

There was concern for a problem with the G-tube placement/leak, so you had a CT scan of your abdomen which was normal and did not show any problems.

summary: You were admitted to the hospital with fevers, a headache, and diarrhea and were found to have a clostridium difficile infection of the gut. We started treated with antiobiotics that needs to be continued for a total of 2 weeks. You were on a medication called omeprazole for GERD/reflux. This medication can increase your risk of clostridium difficile infection, so this was discontinued and replaced with Maalox as needed. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ YO F with chronic cachexia, HTN, GERD, PUD, C diff who presented on ___ for further work up of 3 months of ongoing diarrhea. . # Diarrhea. Patient recently treated for refractory C. diff infection due to persistent dirrhea and positive fecal toxin but without improvement in patient's symptoms. patient refused colonoscopy while in house but agreed to flex sig which was done and which failed to show pseudomembranes but did show a large amount of stool. Given these findings, the patient was thought to be colonized with C. diff and no longer in need of antibiotics. patient was rather thought to be experiencing fecal overflow incontinence as the etiology of patient's diarrhea. The patient refused enemas while in house. patient was therefore placed on a bowel regimen including senna, dulcolax and miralax. One stool culture was sent and was negative for infection as indicated in the labs section of this document. The patient was scheduled with outpatient GI follow up and advised to have a full colonoscopy performed as an outpatient. . # Cachexia, Failure to Thrive. This was discussed with the patient's neice who reported that the patient has always been quite thin and has, in the past, restricted patient's diet to maintain a low BMI. Albumin was normal. patient would benefit from an outpatient nutrition consult and, given patient's significant anxiety as below, a social work or psychiatry referral. . # COPD. Patient unaware of diagnosis which was empirically made when patient recently required intubation back in ___ and given patient's long smoking history. No wheezing on exam and in no distress. . # HTN, CAD. During recent ___ admission, the patient was noted to have had elevated cardiac enzymes and ST elevations on patient's MI with resulting medical management. patient's discharge summary indicates anti-hypertensives and cardioprotective meds which the denies taking. patient also reports normotension at home although patient was hypertensive upon admission and prior to med admin throughout patient's stay. patient was restarted on lisinopril, beta-blockage and ASA 162 mg daily with achievement of normotension prior to discharge. . # Normocytic anemia, guiac positive brown stools. summary: You were admitted to the hospital for evaluation of your diarrhea. You were seen by the Gastroenterologists who recommended that you have a colonoscopy for further diagnostic purposes. Since you declined colonoscopy, you instead had a flexible sigmoidoscopy to evaluate the distal portion of your bowel. The sigmoidoscopy showed lots of stool in your bowel but did not show signs of active C. diff infection. Biopsies were taken and you will be sent the results. You were given medications to help clear out that stool which you should continue. Your dirrhea is likely due to liquid stool passing around more solid stool that is taking up a large portion of your intesting. You should stop taking rifaximin, florastor and vancomycin. You may be colonized with C. diff without active infection although you are still at risk for another infection and so should pay close attention to your symptoms. You were also noted to have high blood pressure. According to your last hospitalization, when you had a heart attack, you were asked to begin taking metoprolol, low dose aspirin, lisinopril and amlodipine. It seems as though you were not taking these at home. You were restarted on metoprolol, low dose aspirin, and lisinopril during this hospitalization and you should continue to take these medications for heart-protective benefits.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ yo patient with 3VD CAD s/p MI in ___, POBA LCX, CHF with EF ___, dyslipidemia, HTN, rheumatic heart disease, AV stenosis s/p valvuloplasty x2 presenting with CHF exacerbation, transferred to ___ for possible repeat valvuloplasty. TTE showed worsening RV function concerning for progression of heart failure. Patient remained on O2 with dyspnea, fatigue, and increasing creatinine. . # Severe AS/CHF (LVEF 25%) - patient is s/p aortic balloon valvuloplasty x 2, presenting with CHF exacerbation. Has already been evaluated by cardiac surgeons who deem patient's extreme risk for conventional aortic valve replacement and was transferred to ___ for possible repeat valvuloplasty as bridge to percutaneous valve replacement. The patient was initially diuresed with home Bumex and IV Lasix and symptoms improved somewhat, with patient requiring only 2L O2. patient's peripheral edema decreased significantly and lungs cleared with only mild-moderate R pleural effusion and very mild bibasilar crackles. However, with diuresis the patient's creatinine increased significantly (1.4-->3.6) and so bumex was held. The patient continued comfortable and without signs of volume overload. It was felt that valvuloplasty would not provide significant improvement of functional status or renal perfusion. Therefore, the patient will continue with medical management until percutanous valve replacement becomes available at ___. For outpatient management of CHF, the pt should be weighed daily, if patient's weight increases by 3lbs or if patient develops SOB not relieved with morphine patient should restart Bumex 1mg daily. . # CP/SOB: The patient presented with CP and SOB. This could be related to worsening RV function, also possible pulmonary process. CXR did not show evidence of pna but did demonstrate pleural effusion and atelectasis. CE continued to decline from admission levels and no change in EKG so not concerned for ACS. PE also low on the differential as patient on subq heparin, no signs of DVT. Could be related to volume overload but hesitant about aggressive diuresis due to increasing creatinine. A component of the SOB was definitly anxiety, which the patient acknowledges. When patient isn't thinking about patient's prognosis patient is able to sit and converse comfortably. Continued to monitor. Treated pain with morphine IV then PO. . UTI: patient complained of dysuria, found to have a UTI. Started on bactrim, completed ___, dysuria decreased. However UCx post-bactrim course grew ___ pansusceptible e.coli. The patient was started on cipro to complete a 7 day course. . # 3VD CAD - s/p MI in ___. Recent POBA to LCx. Continued ASA 81 mg. The patient was started on a low dose beta blocker, initially 12.5mg BID, decreased to 6.25mg BID and then stopped in an effort to increase BP to maintain forward flow for renal perfusion. . # Hyperlipidemia: continued atorvastatin. . # CKD - admitted at baseline of 1.3-1.4, cr increased to 3.6 now 3.2, may be ___ significant diuresis ___, however continued to rise on home bumex. Checked urine lytes (fena >2%) and bladder scan (no retained urine). Pseudo increase of creatinine due to bactrim effect would not explain this elevation. Likely ___ hypoperfusion of kidneys. Renal u/s showed no hydronephrosis, bilateral renal cysts. Renal consulted, recommended holding diuresis, increasing SBPs to >100s, and intervening as soon as possible. Cr is currently trending down, however continues way above baseline. If patient develops clinical signs of heart failure should resume some diuresis, Bumex 1mg as needed, and creatinine should be checked. If pt's cr is increasing with signs of CHF patient should be diuresed more regularly until signs of CHF resolve at which point diuresis can again be held. . # Iron deficiency: continued iron supplements . # Gout: continued allopurinol, changed to renal dosing. . # GERD: continued pantoprazole . # PROPHYLAXIS: DVT ppx with SQ heparin . CODE: DNR/DNI

text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ patient with a history of ulcerative colitis, who presents with 1 week of abdominal pain & diarrhea, and was found to have pancolitis on CT concerning for ulcerative colitis flare. # PANCOLITIS: Patient presented with nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, and a fever to 101.2. Abdominal exam on admission was notable for LLQ tenderness with rebound, mildly and diffusely distended, high-pitched bowel sounds. CT A/P on admission showed bowel wall thickening reflecting pancolitis. CRP 119.1, ESR 41. Initially started on Bactrim/Flagyl but infectious work-up including C. difficile, stool culture, ova and parasites were negative. GI was consulted and recommended flexible sigmoidoscopy which was performed and showed significant colitis consistent with UC with sparing of the rectum (patient on mesalamine enemas). Patient was started on IV methylprednisolone 20mg TID for 3 days then tranitioned to 40mg of prednisone. Screening tests prior to initiation of immunosuppression sent included Hepatits B (neg), Quantiferon gold (neg), and thiopurine methyltransferase (TPMT) enzyme activity (pending at time of discharge). Patient improved significantly while in the hospital. patient's diarrhea resolved, but patient continued to note some minimal hematochezia and mucus in patient's stool, of which GI was made aware. Plan is for follow-up with GI for management of long-term immunosuppression. text: Brief Hospital Course: #. Henoch-Schonlein Purpura with Gastrointestinal, Cutaneous, and Joint Involvement: - GASTROINTESTINAL INVOLVEMENT: Upon admission to the floor, the patient was kept NPO. Solumedrol 20mg IV three-times-a-day was started. Per surgery consult recommendations, cipro and flagyl were started. Pain control with morphine was started, and anti-emetics and a proton pump inhibitor were also given. In addition to surgery, we also consulted dermatology, rheumatology, and gastroenterology. Rheumatology agreed with the plan. Dermatology conducted a skin biopsy with immunohistochemistry, which showed cutaneous IgA deposition (consistent with henoch-schonlein purpura in this clinical setting). Gastroenterology performed an esophagogastroduodenoscopy which was unremarkable. Biopsies were performed as well, and these were also unremarkable. The remainder of the admission was devoted to advancing the diet and transitioning to oral medications. On day 5 of the admission, the patient developed recurrent severe abdominal pain in the context of having advanced the diet to full liquids, become nauseated, & falling behind on oral pain control because of the nausea. The patient was also found to have a leukocytosis to 18.7 and had coincidentally come off cipro/flagyl the night before, although patient was afebrile throughout. Because of this constellation of findings, the patient was given additional pain control (dilaudid, IV morphine) and was sent for abdominal film and abdominal CT and surgery was called. The imaging studies were unremarkable and the patient improved over the course of the day. The patient had a repeat episode of severe abdominal pain at ~1 week, at ~1.5 weeks, at ~2 weeks, and again ~2.5 weeks and patient's pain never fully resolved, always remaining ___. Repeat imaging studies showed interval improvement with decrease inflammation of patient's GI tract seen on CT. The patient's diet was thereafter advanced cautiously. Upon transfer patient was tolerating PO intake with regularly schedule antiemetics. Pain control was transitioned from fully intravenous to part-oral, part-intravenous, to oral-only pain control, however patient continued to experience extreme abdominal pain without many objective findings. Abdominal X-ray showed no free air and abdominal US showed no abnormalities. A pain consult was obtained and recommened starting a PCA so that patient could feel like patient controlled patient's pain herself. At one point patient had been on 60 mg of MSContin tid and a dialudid PCA, however patient became very somnolent and nauseous so patient's MSContin was decreased to 45 mg tid on ___ and the dilaudid PCA was changed to a morphine PCA. patient's settings on transfer were: no basal rate, 1.5 mg IV with a 10 minute lockout (decreased ___ from 2 mg) and a 9 mg hourly limit. Multiple attempts were made at changing patient's IV steroids to PO, however due to patient's continued severe abdominal pain patient was placed back on IV steroids. patient received over two weeks of prednisolone 20 mg IV tid and on ___ it was decided to being tapering. patient is currently on prednisolone 15 mg IV tid. The plan per rheumatology was to decrease patient's prednisolone to 10 mg IV tid on ___. - CUTANEOUS INVOLVEMENT: The patient's rash improved over the course of the admission. Approximately 1 week into the admission, a small area of 1-2mm nonblanching erythematous papules (nearly identical to the initial eruption) was noted on the patient's lower extremities bilaterally. This was thought to be secondary to increased ambulation. Again, about 1.5 weeks into the ___ hospital course, patient developed 1-2mm nonblanching erythematous macules on patient's lower and upper extremities in largely dependent positions. This may have occured in the context of transitioning from IV solumedrol to PO prednisone, or it may be part of the natural course of disease. There was no correlation with worsening or new arthritic, gastrointestional, or renal manifestation of disease. - JOINT INVOLVEMENT: The patient's arthralgias improved significantly over the course of the admission. By a few days into the admission, the patient was observed to be fully ambulatory. The placed on a proton pump inhibitor and Ca/Vit given high dose steroid treatment. #. On the floor, you were continued on antibiotics and steroids, and your breathing continued to improve. You completed your antibiotic course in the hospital, and you will taper down your steroid dose after discharge. Instructions for the steroid taper are attached, but in summary: take 40mg for 2 days (___), 30mg for 2 days (___), 20mg for 2 days (___), 10mg for 2 days (___), and then 10mg every other day (___). Your oxygen level dropped to 83% when you were walking. Because of this we recommend that you use an oxygen tank at home, at least 18 hours per day. We have also added an additional medication called Spiriva to help control your COPD. Please take this in addition to your albuterol and Advair inhalers.

FEV1 43% (Severe). Likely exacerbation precipitated by viral URI. Initially responsive to IV solumedrol and 500 mg azithromycin. However her resp status decompensated and she required hi flow with shovel mask, and despite neb treatments and suctioning, decompensated and required intubation. (the pt reported that she felt worse after she got guaifenesin). She was extubated after less than 24 hours and maintained on neb treatments. Patient was subsequently transferred to the floor in stable condition. On the floor, patient transitioned from IV steroids to PO prednisone 60 QD x5 days (___) to be followed by pred taper. Continued azithro x5 days (___), sputum culture commensal flora. Continued duo-nebs. Patient de-sat'ed on ambulation to 83% so discharged on home O2. # ___: Baseline Cr 0.8, increasing to 1.2. She was treated with gentle hydration and her lisinopril was held. Restarted lisinopril when SBPs>150s. Cre improved to 1.0 by discharge. Chronic Medical Issues: # Hypertension: pt's lisinopril was initially held in the setting of ___, but restarted thereafter when her SBPs >150s. # Hyperlipidemia. Patient on Simvastatin 80 mg. # Anxiety. On paroxetine 40 mg. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: =================== *Spiriva added to home COPD regimen *Pred taper (instructions included for patient) to be completed ___ *Requires home O2 (desat to 83% on ambulation).

text: Brief Hospital Course: ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: ___ with HTN, GERD, Reynauds presenting with atypical chest pain in the setting of a recently normal ETT 1.Chest Pain: Pt Only risk factor is HTN, obesity. Symptomatology is atypical for cardiac cause, except perhaps vasospasm. Patient had negative enzymes, initial EKG showing borderline ST depressions which had resolved in subsequent EKGs, negative stress test and negative CT of the chest. Symptoms sounded almost neurogenic, unclear if past electric exposure caused dysfunction of the peripheral nerves. Nitroglycerin and tramadol did not help patient's pain. Pain was relieved by morphine and ativan initially, valium was the most effective medication at relieving his chest pain,suggesting some anxiety component. Patient also appeared anxious. He has follow up planned with a neuromuscular specialist and will source a cardiologist by referral through his PCP. 2. Hypertension, benign: Continued clonidine, HCTZ.
summary: You were admitted to the hospital because you were having chest pain. You had blood tests, EKGs and a stress test done which showed that you were not having a heart attack and that your chest pain was not related to the heart. You also had a CAT scan of the chest which did not reveal anything abnormal in your lungs or heart. It did show enlargement of your spleen and a fatty liver but these are unlikely the cause of your chest pain.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ year old patient with a history of CAD s/p PCI in ___ with stent to the LAD and RCA, COPD on 2L O2 at night, who initially presented from ___ with concern for ST elevation, s/p cardiac cath without flow limiting disease, sent to the MICU for N/V/D, hypotension, and concern for evolving sepsis. # Hypotension/shock: In the setting of nausea/vomiting/diarrhea and possible pneumonia in the right lower lobe, patient developed hypotension, elevated lactate, and left shift with bandemia, which was concerning for sepsis. Pt was initially treated with IV flagyl and PO vancomycin for presumed C.difficile, until the test came back negative for C.difficile. Urine culture was negative, and blood cultures are still pending. It is likely patient had relative adrenal insufficiency, as patient had just completed a previous steroid taper just prior to admission. PICC line was placed in the MICU for central access. TTE showed normal ejection fraction, making cardiogenic shock less likely. Legionella and stool cultures were all negative. patient was started on ceftriaxone and azithromycin for possible CAP (see below) and on a prednisone taper for relative adrenal insufficiency (also see below). # Community-acquired Pneumonia - Pt was treated for CAP based on chest x-ray findings of opacities, with a 7 day course of ceftriaxone and azithromycin. Pt was initially treated with ceftriaxone through patient's PICC line and then transitioned to cefpodoxime upon discharge. # Coronary vasospasm: Patient has a history of CAD and drug-eluting stent placement to LAD and RCA in ___. Recent catheterization demonstrated minimal coronary disease, without evidence of flow limiting lesions. It is suspected that EKG changes may have been related to vasospasm, as there were no satisfactory alternative explanantions. EKG changes were improved from initial in ___, and troponin post-catheterization was 0.14. Pt was continued on home aspirin, beta-blocker, and statin. patient was also started on diltiazem for vasospasm at 30mg QID and was discharged on the long-acting form of 120mg daily. # COPD/?exacerbation: On 2L home O2 at night, with baseline O2 sat in low to mid ___. patient was continued on patient's home advair, tiotropium, and albuterol. patient was treated for two days with hydrocortisone, equivalent to 40mg prednisone each of those days. After patient was called-out to the regular medicine floor, a steroid taper was initiated of 40mg daily x3 days, 30mg daily x3 days, 20mg daily x3 days, 10mg daily x3 days, 5mg daily x3 days, then 5mg every other day for 5 days. Per OSH records, pt had bronchiectasis seen on chest CT in ___. Patient should be evaluated for possible benefit of flutter valve. # Gastroenteritis: Likely etiology of patient's nausea/vomiting/diarrhea was gastroenteritis, as patient also had a history of sick contacts with similar symptoms. Test was negative for C.difficile infection. After the initial nausea/vomiting/diarrhea resolved, patient began having loose liquid brown stools after initiation of ceftriaxone and azithromycin, though was afebrile with no leukocytosis. patient's loose stools were attributed to side effects of the antibiotics and patient was encouraged to call patient's doctor if the loose stools persist after discontinuation of antibiotics. # ___ secondary to dehydration: Cr 1.8, slightly elevated from baseline 0.8-0.9. Likely etiology was pre-renal in setting of nausea/vomiting/diarrhea as pt came back to baseline upon gentle rehydration. # Anxiety: Pt was continued on home clonazepam, and only required a one-time dose of 0.5mg ativan. # GERD: Pt was continued on home omeprazole. # Hypothyroidism: Pt was continued on home levothyroxine. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES # Please follow-up on patient's downtrending platelets. # Please follow-up on pending blood cultures. # Please assess continuation (if any) of pt's loose stools, that are likely secondary to antibiotics. # Please evaluate patient for possible benefit of flutter valve.
summary: You were admitted for further evaluation of your EKG changes, out of concern for a heart attack. You initially presented to ___ with nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. At ___, there was concern for a heart attack based on changes seen on your EKG (electrocardiogram). You were transferred to ___ for cardiac catheterization. No intervention was performed, as there was good blood flow to your coronary arteries (the blood vessels that supply blood to your heart). It is thought that your EKG changes were due to a spasm in one of your coronary arteries. You were started on a medication, Diltiazem, to help prevent these arteries from spasm. You were also found to have pneumonia (a lung infection) and when you began to have low blood pressures, you were transferred to the intensive care unit for closer monitoring. It is likely that you had low blood pressure in the setting of this infection because your body was not producing enough natural steroids. Therefore, to help your body maintain enough steroids, you were started on prednisone, a steroid medication, which will eventually be tapered off. To treat your pneumonia, you were started on antibiotics. You should continue these antibiotics through ___ (for a total 7-day course).
