text: Brief Hospital Course: ___. patient with CAD s/p CABG on ___, DMII and hypothyroidism presented with nausea, vomiting, and hypotension concerning for sepsis. patient was initially admitted to the MICU for management of severe sepsis. patient was started on broad spectrum antibiotics and fluid resuscitated, pressors were started. RUQ U/S showed gallstones without clear evidence of obstruction; however, due to persistent concern for cholecystitis a percutaneous cholecystomy tube was placed by interventional radiology. Additionally, there were findings concerning for infection at the site of patient's saphenous vein harvest site on the left medial leg. While in the MICU on ___, patient had PEA arrest and underwent 10 minutes of CPR with subsequent ROSC. The etiology of PEA arrest remains unclear--felt to be secondary to hypotension or pulmonary embolism given TTE findings of McConnells sign and dilated right ventricle. However, patient unable to undergo CTA due to acute kidney failure. After CPR, patient was cooled with a goal temperature of 36.5-37 and maintained on pressors and mechanical ventilation. Patient was weaned off pressors and extubated on ___ at which point patient was called out to the general medical floor. On the floor patient was managed supportively. There were several clinical triggers for hypotension and dizziness, usually orthostatic with dizziness. patient responded well to ___ position and very small fluid boluses (250 cc over 30 minutes). Based on the appearance of patient's left lower extremity wounds, a vascular surgery consult was initiated. Arterial studies showed insufficiency of the tibial and popliteal arteries. On ___, patient underwent angioplasty on the left popliteal artery. During the procedure, the surgeon noted purulence in the left lower extremity wounds and drained as much as possible at that time. On ___, vascular surgery took the patient back to the OR for an extensive debridement of the left lower extremity. All necrotic tissue and eschar was removed down to healthy clean subcutaneous tissue. Patient has been stable and with a wound vac placed on the left lower extremity. Tissue was sent from the OR on ___ and did not grow any organisms. On ___, patient had hypotension with systolic blood pressures into the ___ but still mentating, only complaining of dizziness. patient's BP did not respond to fluids immediately and patient was transferred to the MICU for pressors and closer monitoring. In the MICU patient was on phenylephrine for less than an hour before they could be discontinued. An arterial line was placed and demonstrated blood pressures approximately 30 mmHg above noninvasive readings in the right arm. On ___, patient was transferred back to the medical floor from the ICU given patient's clinical stability. Antibiotics were discontinued in the ICU on ___ and the patient has been stable without them since. He blood pressures on the floor have been acceptable in normal range of the patient. Of note, non-invasive blood pressures taken from the right arm continue to be about 30 mmHg lower than pressures measured in other extremities. We recommend confirming blood pressures in at least both arms. ===================== TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: ===================== []CODE STATUS: Full [] If patient appears hypotensive, patient responsive to gentle 250-500 cc IV fluid boluses, **check BP in all four extremities** [] Patient appeared euvolemic at discharge--consider starting Lasix 40 mg PO QDaily if patient becomes volume overloaded (given sCHF) [] Patient discharged on Seroquel 12.5 mg PO QDaily for agitation/delirium. ___ get Seroquel 12.5-25 mg prn for breakthrough if agitated. [] Please have patient follow-up with Dr. ___ (___) in ___ weeks to discuss tube removal and possible cholecystectomy [] Patient will need to continue wound vac to sternotomy and L lower leg wounds until Cardiac Surgery and Vascular Surgery follow-up [] Patient will have Cardiology, Cardiac Surgery, Vascular Surgery, and Neurology followup CODE: Full (confirmed) EMERGENCY CONTACT HCP: ___ (dtr) ___ =============== FLOOR COURSES: ============== ACTIVE ISSUES: ============== # Hypotension: Resolved, now off pressors and stable on small doses of metoprolol. Likely hypovolemic in the setting of diuresis and poor PO intake. Also, MICU noted A-line pressures were 30 mmHg higher than NIBP readings from the right arm. Floor team also notes that BPs in left arm and right leg are significantly higher than those in right arm. Recommend confirming noninvasive BP readings in multiple extremities. Given soft blood pressure, we have deferred starting ACEi for afterload reduction for now; this may be started as an outpatient if able. In addition, we have held diuretics at discharge as the patient was euvolemic. Maintenance Lasix can be restarted based on the discretion of the outpatient providers. If hypotensive, may consider gentle small fluid boluses. # LLE ulceration: Medial necrotic appearing ulcers after saphenous vein harvest. In the setting of likely infection with MSSA. Appearance consistent with vascular insufficiency. Vascular surgery performed angioplasty on popliteal artery. Wounds fully debrided ___ with removal of necrotic tissue, no obvious purulence. Antibiotics discontinued. Continuing wound vac per vascular surgery recommendations. Patient must follow up with vascular surgery. # Glycemic control: Blood sugars have been labile while inpatient. Hypoglycemia resolved now that patient is eating more reliably. Holding patient's home long-acting insulin at time of discharge and maintaining patient on gentle Humalog sliding scale (may increase if needed) and metformin 500mg BID. Of note, patient admitted on long-acting metformin--outpatient providers can consider restarting this formulation. # Mental Status Change: After first MICU course, patient had been somnolent and intermittently confused, off baseline, but this resolved quickly. Alert and oriented x3 when transferred to floor. Etiology thought to be CVA vs. Toxic Metabolic Encephalopathy. Subacute ischemic changes seen on MRI, thought by Neurology to be cardioembolic, likely from chest compressions during PEA arrest. Carotid US showed <40% stenosis. Continued Seroquel 12.5mg standing with Seroquel 25mg BID prn for agitation, anxiety. # sCHF: Last EF=35% from echo on ___. Admitted with ___, EF fell to ___ just after code. Has been difficult to maintain volume status. Lasix prn used for overload: consider maintenance when more stable. Discharged on Metoprolol XL 12.5mg BID. Consider ACEi when stable and BPs can tolerate. # CAD s/p CABG complicated by sternotomy wound dehiscence: Cardiovascular dynamics stable off pressors at time of transfer. Sternotomy wound dehiscence on ___ during code for PEA arrest. Wound vac in place over sternotomy, being managed by Plastic Surgery. Continued aspirin 81 mg daily. Continued atorvastatin 80 mg QPM. Continue wound vac for sternotomy wound with surgical bra to relieve pressure. # Acute Renal Failure: Resolved. Likely ATN secondary to cardiogenic shock. Urine sediment with hyaline casts and muddy brown casts. Improving, with significant auto-diuresis. Creatinine back down to baseline at time of transfer. # Acute cholecystitis (presumed): Patient initially thought to have cholecystitis at time of admission, underwent percutaneous cholecystostomy drainage ___. Patient will need to follow up with interventional radiology for removal of percutaneous cholecystomy tube by early ___. ================ CHRONIC ISSUES: ================ # Hypothyroidism: Continued home Levothyroxine 125mcg # Lymphoma: Stable. s/p Chemo and XRT. = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = ================================================================ ** MICU COURSE ___ ** # s/p PEA arrest: Patient had PEA arrest on ___ and underwent 10 minutes of CPR with subsequent ROSC. patient had a L IJ line placed on ___ and a Swan-Ganz catheter placed via the R IJ. patient had a L femoral arterial line placed for blood pressure monitoring. Given concern for acute blood loss given sternotomy wound dehiscence due to chest compressions, the patient was cooled with a goal temperature of 36.5-37. The precipitant for the patient's arrest was unclear. However, the RV was reportedly underfilled during the arrest, therefore it is possible that a fluid shift caused arrest. TTE showed McConnells sign and dilated RV concerning for PE, therefore patient initially started on heparin gtt. Patient unable to undergo CTA due to renal function. Right lower extremity Doppler negative for DVT; left could not be imaged due to wound. Heparin gtt was subsequently discontinued. patient was intubated during arrest; extubated on ___. # Shock: Likely mixed etiology with septic and cardiogenic components. C. diff was subsequently negative so these antibiotics were discontinued. Initially patient's cardiac output improved with fluid bolus, but then it decreased with subsequent fluid bolus suggestive of cardiogenic shock so patient was initiated on a Lasix gtt. patient's cardiac output subsequently improved with diuresis and patient was able to be weaned from pressors. patient's antibiotics were narrowed to Zosyn. # Toxic Metabolic Encephalopathy: The patient presented with N/V/headache/dizziness. Patient's mental status now improving. # LLE wound: Superficial left lower extremity wound grew MSSA. No evidence of osteomyelitis on imaging. Patient treated with antibiotics as above. Initially treated with Vanc/Zosyn and subsequently narrowed to Zosyn. # ___: Likely secondary to cardiogenic shock as above. Urine sediment with hyaline and muddy brown casts consistent with ATN. # Acute cholecystitis: Initial RUQ ultrasound consistent with evidence of acute cholecystitis given gallbladder distention, cholelithiasis and sludge, gallbladder wall edema, and mild pericholecystic free fluid, for which patient underwent percutaneous drainage of patient's gallbladder. = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = ================================================================ *** MICU COURSE ___ *** # Hypotension: Responded well to 500cc bolus. patient was pancultured for repeat infectious workup. Antibiotics were held pending culture data. Captopril was discontinued in the setting of hypotension. A-line placed. Invasive pressure monitoring approximately 30 points higher than non-invasive monitoring. # LLE Wound: s/p revascularization, debridement per vascular surgery. Vascular surgery notified of new admission to MICU and concern for left lower extremity as potential source of infection. On their evaluation after taking down wound vac, wound bed looks clean, no prurulence. New cultures sent. Antibiotics held for now to allow patient to declare infection. # Pleural effusions: Bilateral, possibly from heart failure, low albumin state, acute illness. Patient without any respiratory distress. On crosssectional imaging from ___, effusions were not loculated. Diuretics held for now given overall picture concerning for low volume state. # Mental Status Changes: Patient has been somnolent and intermittently confused, off baseline, but felt to be resolving, likely toxic metabolic encephalopathy. Subacute ischemic changes seen on MRI, thought by Neurology to be cardioembolic, likely from chest compressions during PEA arrest. Carotid US showed <40% stenosis. With improved blood pressure, mental status improved. patient was continued on Seroquel 12.5 mg standing with PRN for agitation or anxiety. # Type II DM: Labile blood sugars. Hypoglycemia on the floor, hyperglycemia here. Long acting insulin held per floor team. Insulin sliding scale uptitrated for hyperglycemia. Will ultimately likely need re-initiation of long acting insulin. # sCHF: Last ___ from echo on ___, just after code. Admitted with ___. Has been difficult to maintain volume status. Final read ECHO pending. ACEi, beta blocker, and diuretics on hold for now. # CAD s/p CABG: Cardiovascular dynamics stable off pressors at time of transfer. Sternotomy wound dehiscence on ___ during code for PEA arrest. Labetalol held in the MICU. Continued on aspirin and atorvastatin. # Acute cholecystitis: Patient initially thought to have cholecystitis, underwent perc chole drainage ___, continue ___ weeks. - Ongoing drainage - Patient will need to follow up for removal of perc chole tube in early ___ >30 minutes spent coordinating discharge to rehab
summary: As you know, you were admitted with low blood pressure. We felt you had a left leg infection and possibly an infection in your gallbladder. You were treated with antibiotics and fluids. You also experienced a cardiac arrest in the intensive care unit (ICU) and received medications to support your blood pressure and heart. For your leg infection, you had a procedure to remove dead and infected tissue. You had a wound vacuum to help the wound heal better. You also had a tube placed to for inflamed gallbladder which you will need removed in several weeks. We stopped some of your medications because of low blood pressure.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ year old F with polysubstance abuse including alcohol, insulin dependent diabetes mellitus is admitted to MICU with upper GI bleed, ETOH intoxication and transaminities. . # GI Bleed: Thought to be upper GI bleed given hematemsis and dark stool. EGD showed no obvious source of bleeding. . # DKA: Patient was initially on insulin gtt. This was titrated off, and patient was transferred out of the ICU to the general medicine floor. Reviewed recent OSH imaging which raised concern for abnormality at prior nephrectomy site, but was otherwise unremarkable for acute abdominal process. OSH images were reviewed with patient outpatient's urologist, who felt no acute changes were present on CT images and that no additional imaging of the area was indicated. Patient reported patient wanted to defer this until after patient's upcoming shoulder surgery. GI recommended against further inpatient GI workup. text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ yo patient with h/o recurrent C. diff s/p fecal transplant (___), IBS and GERD who presented with diarrhea, abdominal pain and sinus tachycardia found to have severe C diff pancolitis. # C. DIFF PANCOLITIS: Initial labs showed leukocytosis 28.3 with bandemia, ___ showed diffuse colonic mucosal thickening without e/o megacolon, C. diff assay positive. In the MICU, patient was started on high-dose Vanco 500mg PO q6 hrs and Flagyl 500mg IV q8 hrs in light of patient's severe recurrent C diff. patient required high doses of IV narcotis for pain control, and received aggressive IV fluid due to severe diarrhea and resultant tachycardia. patient was seen by both acute care surgery and gastroenterology while in the ICU. Administration of IVIG was discussed, not favored by GI given lack of evidence supporting its efficacy. patient's abdominal pain and leukocytosis improved moderately, at which point patient was transferred to medical floor. On the floor, patient had ongoing pain requiring frequent narcotics and was still having 8 stools per day. ID was consulted regarding possibility of starting Fidoxamycin, felt this was not indicated on inpatient basis as Fidoxamycin has not been studied in this specific population so no evidence it would help. Per GI recs, Vanco was tapered to 125mg PO q6 hrs as patient did not have e/o ileus. patient will complete one-month course of Vanco 125mg PO q6 hrs, and then complete long slow Vanco taper as directed by patient's outpatient GI Dr. ___. patient continued IV Flagyl as well per GI recs, on discharge switched to PO Flagyl. Dr. ___ determine whether to continue Flagyl at patient's upcoming follow-up appointment. On discharge, patient's stool frequency had decreased to 4 per day and patient's abdominal pain was continuing to improve. # HEMATOCHEZIA: Patient's HCT drifted down over the course of hospitalization, from 43 on admission to 26 on discharge. Much of this was likely dilutional from the large amount of IV fluids patient received. However, patient also c/o BRBPR when on the floor. To rule out possibility of co-existing infectious, inflammatory or ischemic colitis, flexible sigmoidoscopy was performed on ___. It showed diffuse continuous ulceration, friability, erythema, hemorrhages and pseudomembranes with contact bleeding, c/w severe C diff colitis. Findings explained likely etiology of patient's BRBPR. Also checked stool cx and O/P to rule out superinfection, all negative. BRBPR resolved without intervention and HCT stabilized. # SINUS TACHYCARDIA: In the MICU, patient was tachycardic to >150 secondary to hypovolemia, pain and anxiety, improved to 140s with IVF and lorazepam PRN. Considered PE, found unlikely because never hypoxic. TSH WNL. HR slowly trended down over the course of hospitalization with volume repletion and pain management, 90-100 on discharge. # DELIRIUM: On HD#2 while in MICU, patient became acutely delirious with worsening sinus tachycardia. patient's sister and boyfriend admitted at that time that patient typically drinks ___ beers/day most days of week, so patient was started on CIWA scale. patient required both Haldol and CIWA with benzodiazepines. Mental status improved by HD#3. Afterward, patient and family all vehemently denied h/o alcohol abuse. Social work consult was obtained to further explore this issue, patient declined any further support or counseling for the question of alcohol abuse. patient was started on thiamine, multivitamin and folate during hospitalization and on discharge. # ___ EDEMA: pt developed 2+ BLE pitting edema to thighs over first week of hospitalization, likely ___ large volume IVF received. Gradually improved with autodiuresis, compression stockings and leg elevation and had completely resolved by discharge. #GERD: continued home omeprazole and ranitidine per Dr. ___ ___. Considered DC'ing given increased risk of C diff but given pt's h/o significant GERD felt best to continue these. #RA: initially held home meloxican ___ ___, restarted before discharge. Continued home hydroxychloroquine. #IBS: initially held home Bentyl, restarted upon discharge. #ADHD: continued home Venlafaxine. Held home amphetamine-dextroamphetamine during hospitalization, restarted on discharge. =============================== TRANSITION OF CARE: -Studies pending on discharge: colon biopsies from flex sig
summary: You were admitted to the hospital with diarrhea and abdominal pain. You were found to have recurrent C. difficile infection causing pancolitis (inflammation of your entire large intestine). You were admitted to the ICU and started on antibiotics and IV fluids, then transferred to the regular medical floor once your condition had stabilized. You continued to improve and the frequency of your bowel movements continued to decrease. You also had blood in your stool so Flexible Sigmoidoscopy was performed, with findings consistent with C diff pan-colitis.

text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is an ___ yo patient with history of hypertension, anxiety, dementia, chronic hyponatrmia who presents for new onset seizures in the setting of two weeks of altered mental status. patient had head CT that was negative. patient was placed on continuous EEG which initially showed periodic lateralized epileptic discharges and several seizures. patient was started on keppra, clobazam and phenytoin, which resulted in seizure control. patient was started on empiric bacterial and viral meningitic coverage. patient underwent lumbar puncture which showed lymphocytic pleocytosis and 13 WBCs. patient underwent MRI brain w/ and w/o contrast, which showed increased signal in the meninges over the L temporal, L parietal areas. Initially there was concern for viral encephalitides. Following LP results bacterial antibiotic coverage was discontinued given relatively few WBCs. Acyclovir was continued until HSV PCR returned negative. Other viral PCRs (EBV, HSV, VZV, CMV) have returned negative as well. CSF culture was negative. patient's MRI showed multiple areas of punctate susceptibility artifact compatible with probable cerebral amyloid angiopathy, given the FLAIR signal in patient's meninges and presentation of seizures, diagnosis of inflammatory cerebral angiopathy was considered most likely, as patient's mental status did not improve as would be expected and viral meningitis and other workup was negative. It is possible the inflammatory component could have been triggered by patient's UTI. text: Brief Hospital Course: Shortness of breath from presumed acute on chronic diastolic congestive heart failure exacerbation: Patient with documented history of shortness of breath for last month responsive to diuretics. Additionally, appeared volume overloaded on physical exam with JVP to 8cm, +1 peripheral edema, and diffuse crackles with evidence of volume overload on CXR. Lack of fevers/chills, and consistency of symptoms for last month with response to diuretics made infectious cause such as PNA less likely. Diuresed piecemeal with 40 mg IV lasix boluses. Patient with adequate UOP. Watched kidney function with slow trend up in creatinine from 0.8 to 1.0. Also noted to be alkalemia with HCO3 on CMP seen to be in the mid 30___. SOB resolved with O2 requirement titrated down from 5L on presentation to 1L. Discharged on medical regimen of beta blocker, lisinopril, and Lasix 80 mg PO daily. *Follow up CMP within 3 days of discharge PUMP: Came in with clinical presentation of heart failure exacerbation. Had repeat echocardiography which illustrated slightly more enlarged RV but otherwise unchanged from prior echo six months ago, with preserved EF at 55% with evidence of diastolic dysfunction. Was diuresed per above, and continued on BB as well as ACE-I. Considered starting on aldactone but given low BP's, borderline hyperkalemia, and no evidence of benefit in patient's with diastolic dysfunction, did not initiate. *Will need follow up of clinical presentation to check for fluid overload (diffuse crackles & rhonchi throughout) *Should titrate furosemide dose or resume combination with metolazone 30 minutes prior to loop diuretic for synergistic diuretic effect. RHYTHM: Pacemaker in place for h/o symptomatic bradycardia with history of atrial fibrillation as well. Stable. Did not appear to be in afib w/ RVR. No evidence of anticoagulation with atrial fibrillation history. CHADS2 of ___ (questionable stroke). Will continue to hold anticoagulation as unclear why not on it; presumed to be due to high fall risk, but it should be readdressed with cardiologist/PCP & health care proxy. Continued on beta blocker and remained ventricularly paced during hospital stay with occassional junctional beats. UTI: UA showed evidence of UTI. Last micro data grew E.Coli resistant to ciprofloxacin. Gave Bactrim DS bid for 3 days. Was asymptomatic and afebrile during hospitalization. *Follow up UA for resolution of pyuria. *Follow up blood cutlures/urine cultures Leukopenia/anemia: Unlcear etiology. White count was documented at 3.9 in ___. Cell counts stable. ___ be bone marrow suppressive effect/early MDS. ___ be low in presence of infection, given florid UTI. Review of medication list shows low likelihood of leukopenia from simvastatin, agranulocytosis from metoprolol, and agranulocytosis/leukopenia/aplastic anemia from furosemide. Bactrim ___ also cause synthetic dysfunction/myelosuppression. Given chronicity of medications, kept current regimen with monitoring for worsening cell counts. Remained stable in house. *Follow up CBC Anxiety/insomnia: Patient became very agitated on HD#2 with requests to go home and trying to leave the floor. Documentation showed use of clonazepam at nursing facility. Given increased risk of worsening delirium/agitation, avoided using benzodiazepine. Controlled agitation with IV/PO haloperidol, as well as sublingual olanzapine with good response. Attempted to decrease abetting factors of delirium by removing foley catheter and establishing reorienting cues and having ___ interperters aid in reorientation. *Consider using Haldol for agitation in acute situations *Would use clonazepam with caution, as ___ increase delirium/agitation in elderly patients. CHRONIC ISSUES HTN: Normotensive in house on low dose lisinopril. OA: pain control with tylenol and lidocaine patch TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: Per above. Difficult to control fluid status. Would endorse a fluid restricted diet with <2 liters free water per day. Would also place on sodium restricted diet and weigh daily to clinically monitor signs of worsening heart failure. Re: Agitation/Insomnia, ___ want to try different sleep aid such as trazodone at night, as benzodiazepines can worsen agitation. As patient is established on this therapy at patient's nursing home, discharged to use 0.5 mg qhs for insomnia. Also gave prescription for 0.5 mg haloperidol PO TID for agitation. Re: UTI, follow up UA. PENDING LABS: Blood Cultures; preliminary urine culture growing E.coli

summary: You were admitted to the hospital because of sensory changes involving your face, leg and arm. Your symptoms were not associated with any headache, but you were anxious at the time. The symptoms resolved by the time you were admitted. Because of concern for stroke, you had imaging which did not reveal any acute abnormalities, which was reassuring. We did not start any new medications or perform any procedures during this admission. It is unclear why you had these symptoms. It is possible you had some mild cerebral hypoperfusion (pre-syncope or almost fainting) which caused the symptoms, or that you had an atypical migraine headache. Anxiety may also have played a role. We are reassured that you did not have any findings suggestive of stroke or brain lesion. We will discharge you home on your home medications.

It is normal to feel anxious or stressed by major events such as being in the hospital. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ yo F, former smoker admitted with subacute, progressive dyspnea on exertion. The patient presented for further evaluation of patient's subacute, progressive dyspnea on exertion. patient had recently undergone an extensive negative outpatient and inpatient (at ___ ___) work-up including normal lab work, cardiac enzymes, d-dimer, chest x-ray, pulmonary function testing (note made of slight mid-expiratory flow slowing) and stress testing (note made of poor visualization of the inferior myocardium). patient had recently been started on albuterol and advair for a component of reactive airway disease or asthma. There was no clear acute change in the patients condition on history though patient did note some worsened congestion since starting advair. The patient had normal labs including chem 7, CBC, BNP (of 47) and multiple sets of negative cardiac enzymes. EKG revealed some t wave flattening across the precordium of non-specific, unclear significance. CXR and CTA were negative for an acute pulmonary process including infiltrate, PE or dissection. The patient had an echo which was witnin normal limits. patient ambulated with patient's nurse and was found to have resting oxygen saturation 94% on room air to 92% with exertion and subjective dyspnea. patient continued on albuterol PRN during patient's hospitalization. Your bilirubin began rising and an ultrasound showed a blockage of bile ducts. A bile duct drain was placed. However, this procedure did not reduce the bilirubin, implying that the blockage was not relieved or that the liver was failing. During that procedure, the radiologists noted that the pancreatic cancer had continued to spread to the small bowel as well as the liver. The decision then was made to focus on keeping you comfortable. Arrangements were made to send you home with hospice support. Antibiotics started for a possible infection of the bile ducts (cholangitis) were stopped when you left the hospital.

text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ right-handed patient with history notable for prior TBI c/b convergence spasm and post-traumatic headaches, anxiety, insomnia, somatoform disorder, and intractable migraines s/p botulinum toxin injections and occipital nerve blocks presenting for evaluation of headache and visual disturbance. patient was noted to have new papilledema since patient's prior documented evaluation last ___, with associated splinter hemorrhages, raising concerns for intracranial hypertension as the etiology of patient's headaches. CTA/CTV reassuringly did not reveal evidence of venous sinus thrombosis. patient underwent ___ guided LP which revealed an opening pressure of >50. 34 cc of CSF was drained and closed with a pressure of 16. Neuro ophthalmology was consulted and Dr. ___ patient's in his office soon after admission. Visual acuity testing revealed patient's best corrected distance to be ___ in each eye. Funduscopy revealed Frisen 2 (possibly trace Frisen 3) papilledema ___ with extensive peripapillary RNFL heme OS>OD. Automated perimetry revealed mild inferior loss and blind spot enlargement OD>OS. LP revealed OP > 50 with normal constituents. patient was started on oral Topamax initially given the relative contraindication for acetazolamide with the history of nephrolithiasis. patient noted some improvement in headache and visual changes after initial LP but patient's symptoms gradually worsened over the next ___ hours. Acetazolamide was added and serial visual field testing was done which showed some worsening in visual fields which is likely a sign of increased intracranial pressures. Topamax and acetazolamide doses were increased to optimize therapy and neurosurgery consulted for lumbar drain placement. patient was transferred to Neuro ICU for closer monitoring. In the NeuroICU, only about 1cc of fluid drained from the lumbar drain. Neurosurgery was notified and they tried to adjust the drain, but the drain was deemed non-functional. Visual fields remained unchanged during this period. Lumbar drain was removed and patient was called back out to the floor. On the floor, note was made of acidemia and hypochloremia on acetazolamide, which was discontinued in consultation with Nephrology, who recommended addition of potassium citrate for prevention of kidney stones. Topiramate was uptitrated in lieu of acetazolamide, and visual fields were noted to be stable off acetazolamide. A short course of added baclofen was added for cervicalgia contributing to the headaches, and recommendation was made for bariatric surgery on follow-up. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES 1. Check basic chemistry profile in one week to evaluate for hyperkalemia. 2. Avoid future use of retinoic acid products, consider switching to non-estrogen based contraceptive strategies. 3. You were admitted to the hospital and started on medication called topiramate and acetazolamide. You were also seen by neuro-ophthalmology (Dr. ___ and your visual fields were tested. You were noted to have some decrease in vision and with repeated testing it was noted to be getting slightly worse. You underwent lumbar drain placement to help drain the CSF fluid gradually, but the lumbar drain was not successful. Your vision remained stable. You had a subsequent LP in the setting on consistent headaches and lack vision loss since initial improvement no admission, with no relief of headaches or further improvement in visual symptoms. Your Acetazolamide was discontinued in the setting of lack of clinical benefit with academia and hypo-chloremia, and your topiramate dose was increased instead. Your visual fields remained stable, and discussion about weight loss and life style modifications to help permanently treat your IIH. You met with a nutritionist during patient's hospitalization to review dietary techniques. We are also arranging for you to meet with the bariatric surgeon for long-term weight loss plans. Post-cath EKG revealed residual mild ST-segment elevations in the inferior leads. ECHO at outside hospital revealed that patient's MI had caused significant RV dysfunction and failure, causing dilation and tricuspid regurgitation. Repeat ECHO at ___ confirmed right ventricular cavity dilation with depressed free wall contractility and severe [4+] tricuspid regurgitation. Pt also underwent stress EKG and ECHO to evaluate for residual ischemia. Stress EKG revealed no significant ST segment changes during exercise or in recovery. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ year-old patient transferred to ___ for evaluation of elevated D-dimer in the setting of lightheadedness, right-sided chest pain, and lip tingling. The principle concern was for pulmonary embolism given the elevated D-dimer, which is very nonspecific. The patient has no risk factors for developing a DVT. patient is very active in patient's daily life and is rarely ever sedentary. patient has only had two incidences of lightheadedness and they were self-limited (lasting only ___ minutes) and always associated with a stressful day. The patient's chest pain on the right side is very consistent with abdominal muscle strain given that the patient just started doing vigorous abdominal crunch exercises just two days prior to the onset of right-sided rib cage pain. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ yo F with h/o bipolar disorder, anxiety, hypothyroidism with recent aspiration PNA/UTI presenting after being found down at home with ?cerebellar lesion. # Altered mental status- Patient had waxing and waning mental status throughout admission, but gradually had improving in daytime wakefulness. No infectious source was localized, patient had no evidence of seizures on continuous EEG, and CT and MRI showed no evidence of hemorrhage (but did note presence of benign cavernoma). In addition, lithium level was appropriate, so unlikely to be lithium toxicity, and TSH was also normal. Neurology followed patient throughout admission and felt that somnolence and delerium was likely related to high doses of zyprexa and trazodone. Per patient's outpatient psychiatrist, in the past, bad insomnia has triggered severe psychosis/mania, leading to high doses of trazodone (150mg qHS). Trazodone was held on admission, and patient had no issues with sleep. We will suggest to continue the medication on an as needed basis only. In addition, zyprexa was titrated down to 10mg qHS, and the 2.5mg BID was continued. Outpatient psychiatrist agreed that this should be titrated down, however, patient had met resistance from the family in the outpatient setting, mostly due to fear of mania. Patient remained stable during admission, despite lowered dosing. Patient was at patient's baseline mental status, per family, at the time of discharge. patient was difficult to arouse at times during the morning, but quickly cleared and became interactive and oriented. patient was never oriented to specific place, or time. We continued to provide frequent reorientation. # Left supraspinatous tear- Patient had decreased range of motion, and tenderness to palpation over left anterior shoulder on admission. There was an area of focused erythema anteriorly as well, concerning for potential hemarthrosis v septic arthritis. Patient was evaluated by rheumatology who felt that erythema was likely related to fall; main concerns being hemarthrosis and tear of tendon. MRI confirmed tendon tear, without evidence of hemarthrosis. Per orthopedics, patient is not a surgical candidate. Physical therapy worked with patient and gave exercises to be continued and rehab and following discharge. Patient also has follow-up scheduled with orthopedics. There was swelling on the left extremity as well, with intact radial pulses. This was thought to be due to immobilization of arm in setting of significant pain. An ultrasound showed no evidence of deep vein thrombosis. # Hypernatremia- Patient with long-term use of lithium likely has underlying diabetes inspidius, and in hospital setting was not taking normal amount of free water. # Cerebellar lesion- Incidental finding on MRI of right cerebellar cavernoma on MRI without hemorrhage. This is a benign process that needs no intervention, but should be followed as outpatient as there is a 2% risk of bleed. # Bipolar disorder- Patient usually very manic, has not been hospitalized for ___ years per daughter-in-law. Lithium level appropriate at 0.7 at outside hospital. As above, concern that insomnia often triggers mania; however outpatient psychiatrist was very in favor of titrating down on zyprexa and trazodone. # GERD- Continued home omeprazole 20mg po BID # Hypothyroidism- TSH 1.43, within normal limits, at outside hospital. Continued home levothyroxine 50mcg po daily # Transitional issues- - patient will need outpatient follow-up with psychiatrist upon discharge from rehab: Dr. ___ in ___ ___ - neurology follow-up scheduled to monitor cavernoma - orthopedics follow-up scheduled for supraspinatous tear; please see physical therapy recommendations for daily exercises on left shoulder. - concern for trazodone causing delerium and increased risk of falls; please only dose if necessary for insomnia (increased risk of mania with insomnia) - tamsulosin discontinued given concern for increased risk of falls; if worsening urinary frequency, may restart
summary: You were admitted because of a fall at home, and being unable to get up. You did not have a bleed in your brain. You also likely did not have a seizure. We are concerned that some of your medications have been making it difficult for you to walk, and we decreased and stopped these medications. An MRI of your brain showed a benign lesion called a cavernoma. This should be watched by your primary care doctor. In addition, you injured your left arm.

text: Brief Hospital Course: BRIEF SUMMARY ============= ___ y/o F with morbid obesity, DM2 (on insulin), h/o sigmoid colon CA s/p open sigmoid colectomy (___) c/b wound dehicence and chronic nonhealing ventral wound who re-presented to ED following recent admission ___ with abdominal discomfort and leg edema/pain. ACUTE ISSUES: # Hypervolemia - Patient came in with pitting edema throughout patient's legs, groin and abdomen. This was thought to be due to missing home doses of lasix during patient's recent admission. patient has elevated BNP of 1323, though no prior BNP in OMR. Lasix was restarted, dose was increased and patient diuresed well. patient's edema improved. There was a concern for a component of heart failure, so an echocardiogram was done. The TTE was of poor quality d/t patient's habitus, but it revealed no frank evidence of heart failure. patient required PRN doses of lasix 40mg IV for diuresis. patient was encouraged to decrease patient's fluid intake (patient endorsed drinking ___ glasses per day). On discharge, patient's home lasix was increased to 40 mg from 20 mg. # Abdominal Wound - The patient has a non-healing wound from patient's surgery for which patient was recently admitted. The fluid from the wound was always serosanguinous, never any purulent discharge. The patient did not have signs or symptoms of infection. It is suspected that patient has poor healing due to low albumin and significant edema/turgor. patient's chronic abdominal wound was draining fluid, so patient was seen by colorectal surgery who placed a wound vac resulting in serosanguinous fluid output. There was no concern for infection from either the surgical or medical team. The wound vac dysfunctioned multiple times in that it had trouble adhering to the patient and maintaining adequate pressure. One evening, this resulted in the patient having a mechanical fall due to slipping in some of the wound fluid. The patient was stable, but did experienced some soreness in patient's abdomen after the fall. # Bilateral Leg Pain - The patient came in with leg pain and erythema. This was though to be due to worsening stasis dermatitis. patient received one dose of vancomycin in the ED, but this was stopped after arrival on the floor. patient was treated with topical clobetasol, kerlix, ACE wrap and elevation of legs. # Impaired Renal Function - The patient was discharged with a Cr of 2.2 from patient's recent hospitalization and found to have a Cr of 1.5 on admission. This was thought to be due to resolving pre-renal acute kidney injury from patient's last hospitalization. patient had some urinary frequency which was attributed to baseline stress incontinence and diuresis with lasix. By the end of patient's hospitalization, patient's creatinine had decreased to 1.3. # Positive UCx - During a work-up for the patient's abdominal pain, patient was found to have a urine culture which was positive for Klebsiella. This was possibly contaminated with skin/genital flora, but the decision was made, however, to treat this as symptomatic bacteriurea as symptoms could have been vague in this patient given baseline feeling of incomplete bladder emptying and reasons for polyuria (lasix). patient received three days of ciprofloxacin which patient finished as an outpatient. CHRONIC ISSUES: # Morbid obesity - Stable. Patient has a BMI of 84. Was previously exploring bariatric surgery, but diagnosis/treatment of colon cancer has delayed this. Discharged with physical therapy recommendations. # HTN - Normotensive during hospital stay. Home lisinopril was continued. # Colon CA - Stable. Stopped Capecitabine in ___, per patient. Seen by colorectal surgery and outpatient follow-up was advised. # IDDM - On last discharge/admission and per patient, patient was using Lantus 90U BID, Metformin 1g BID, Glipizide 10mg BID at home. patient's metformin and glipizide were held in the setting of ___, and patient was managed with sliding scale insulin and Glargine 80 U BID. Follow-up with ___ was recommended. # Anxiety - Patient experienced moderate anxiety surrounding patient's inpatient stay. patient was given PRN ativan and required much reassurance about patient's treatment course. Outpatient psychiatric follow-up is recommended. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: - please continue to titrate lasix dose for diuresis - please keep wound vac in place; patient can follow-up with colorectal surgery - please follow Cr and electrolytes for resolution ___ - follow-up with ___ for outpatient diabetes management - code: full - contact: ___ ___ ___ on Admission: The Preadmission Medication list is accurate and complete. 1. Acetaminophen 1000 mg PO Q8H:PRN pain 2. Docusate Sodium 100 mg PO BID 3. Fluconazole 200 mg PO Q24H 4. Thiamine 100 mg PO DAILY 5. MedroxyPROGESTERone Acetate 10 mg PO ONCE DAILY FOR 10 DAYS AT THE END OF EACH MONTH 6. Magnesium Oxide 400 mg PO DAILY 7. Lisinopril 10 mg PO DAILY 8. Furosemide 20 mg PO DAILY 9. Vitamin D 50,000 UNIT PO Q2WEEKS 10. GlipiZIDE 10 mg PO BID
summary: You were admitted to the hospital for care of your surgical wound and concern for skin infection. Your surgical wound was found to be draining normal fluid, so a wound vac was placed on it to help drain the fluid and promote healing. Your legs were found to have a skin condition called stasis dermatitis, which is an inflammation of the skin related to fluid overload in your veins. You were treated for this excess fluid with an increase in your diuretic. Your urinary frequency was probably related to the use of diuretics, however, we did find evidence of bacteria in your urine, which can also cause urinary frequency. For this, you were treated with a course of antibiotics, which you completed as an inpatient.

By the time of discharge patient had received 4 days of vanc/cefepime with improvement in patient's symptoms (unclear if causal). text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ y/o F with a h/o Dementia, severe constipation identified recent admission for encephalopathy, HTN, who presents from patient's nursing home for altered mental status. ACTIVE ISSUES ===================== # Encephalopathy, Dementia, Goals of care: Presented with several days of lack of PO intake, and decline from baseline level of functioning. Although etiology of patient's encephalopathy and decline remains unclear, patient's current mental status more likely represents decline of patient's underlying dementia, given no other clear source was identified. Infectious workup was negative, electrolyte abnormalities were corrected, thyroid studies were improved, head CT was negative, and constipation was treated. Family meeting on ___ made decision to make patient comfort measures only. There was some improvement in mental status on ___, and family elected to keep low rate IV fluids running at that time. On ___, fluids were stopped and family elected to trial PO intake for comfort, accepting of aspiration risks. Palliative Care was consulted, who helped the family discuss through their goals of care, and the decision was made to continue comfort measures only, and to pursue hospice care. MOLST form filled out, stating DNR, DNI, Do Not Hospitalize. PO medications were discontinued due to aspiration risk, but the patient may continue to eat PO as tolerated for comfort. # Constipation: Presented with at least 3 days of constipation. Prior admission was complicated by severe constipation, with CT findings of "Distal sigmoid and rectum massively distended with stool measuring up to 10.8 x 10.1 cm." Cannot take PO medications for bowel regimen due to poor swallowing function. ___ XR with large stool burden, though no e/o obstruction. After goals of care change, routine temperature monitoring was not pursued. # Hypernatremia: presented with Na of 146, then received 1L NS, then 148. Most likely due to poor PO intake and lack of free water. patient's sodium gradually improved with half-normal saline, most recently 142. Speech and Swallow team consulted, recommending NPO and no PO meds. Patient was not requiring any of these medications for the days prior discharge, but could in the future. - Pt noted to have Conjunctivitis. Was started on Erythromycin ointment, four times daily, on ___. Please continue this medication through ___, to complete a 7 day course. Treating this infection is consistent with goals of care, given that eye infection produces discomfort. - DNR/DNI, Comfort Measures Only, Do Not Hospitalize

text: Brief Hospital Course: ## Flank pain: Unclear etiology. CT ABD showed 5mm R sided non-obstructing kidney stone. patient had a CTA Chest that did not show any large central PEs or pulmonary process that could explain this pain. Possible pain represents muscle strain from being in bed. Pain controlled with Ultram 50 mg TID, Flexerel 10 mg TID, Tylenol, and Lidocaine patches. Additionally, Clonidine 0.2 mg TID helped patient's with patient's anxiety. Notably, patient very fixated on pain and multiple times per day would request uptitration of tramadol. Given unclear source we maintained the above regimen and firmly tried not to give any narcotics. . ## Hypoxia/Bronchospasm: Patient had an episode of desatting to the ___ hosp day #2. This was presumed bronchospasm, secondary to Ketorolac which patient was given for patient "kidney pain." It may have also been a COPD flare, but patient did not have any productive sputum. A CTA was performed which ruled out any large PE or other new pulmonary process. Patient was gradually weaned from 5 L to Room Air, and was also treated with nebulizers, albuterol, and oral steroids. patient is now stable at 95% on RA. patient will be another two days of steroids and can then stop. patient should continue on albuterol and advair inhalers as prescribed. . ## Alcoholic Hepatitis: Patient was admitted with significantly elevated ASTs and ALTs, characteristic of alcoholic hepatitis. These have trended down significantly since admission. patient was also tested for HIV (pending), and Hepatitis A, B, and C. patient has been vaccinated for Hep A in the past, and is Hep C positive. We would suggest that patient see a hepatologist after patient is discharged from psych facility. . # Leukocytosis: Likely secondary to steroids. No fevers or positive culture results. . ## Hypothyroidism: Patient had been found to have a TSH above assay from patient's OSH, and was started on Synthroid which was continued throughout this stay. patient will need a TSH checked in about 6 weeks so that dose can be uptitrated as needed. . # Transient Hyperglycemia: Likely secondary to steroids. Single blood sugar above 200 otherwise within a normoglycemic range. No need for further management. . ## Hepatitis C: VL 126 K. CEA and AFP were checked and within normal range. Pt has never had treatment for Hep C in the past. patient should be followed by a hepatologist and will need help finding a doctor. patient should at some point be vaccinated for Hepatitis B, this could be done by PCP. ## Psych: Patient has extensive polysubstance abuse history, and had just completed patient's Methodone taper at ___. patient had 2 more days of Librium taper to complete here, which patient did at 50 mg one day, and 25 mg the second. Psychiatry followed patient's closely during inpt stay. Psychiatry feels patient meets ___ criteria for transfer back to inpatient psych.

You do have a right sided kidney stone but this should not be causing you pain. It is possible this represents a muscle strain. We have treated you with Ultram, Tylenol and a muscle relaxor. You began very short of breath which may have been due to a pain medication we gave you. We treated you with nebulizers and steroids and your breathing stabilized.

text: Brief Hospital Course: A ___ year-old man with history of EtOH abuse, cirrhosis secondary to hepatitis C infection, portal hypertension with esophageal varices, and thrombocytopenia who is presenting from home with right arm motor neuropathy, rhabdomyolysis, and EtOH withdrawal after passing out on the floor on his right arm for ___ days. . 1. Right arm motor weakness. He was seen by neurology in the emergency department who felt that his symptoms were consistent with radial nerve palsy, or ___ night palsy," due to prolonged pressure on the radial nerve when he was passed out from EtOH. They recommended for ___ referral and tylenol prn for pain control. Once the C-spine CT returned negative for fracture, his neck collar was removed. . He had subtle improvement in right hand symptoms overnight, but full recovery of motor function and finger range of motion ___ likely take weeks. He ___ follow-up for outpatient physical therapy. . 2. EtOH withdrawal. He was started on CIWA scale for withdrawal symptoms. He was also given multivitamin, folate and thiamine supplements. His withdrawal symptoms had improved at time of discharge, and his CIWA scores were consistently less than 10. Our social worker met with him and provided contact information for several rehab programs in the area of ___, where he lives. . 3. Rhabdomyolysis. Patient presented with CK of 1631 that came down with intravenous fluids. His creatinine was stable. . 4. Portal hypertension/esophageal varices. We continued his outpatient nadolol. . 5. History of hepatic encephalopathy. His ammonia level was 44. We continued his outpatient Xifaxin. . 6. Pancytopenia. He was noted to have pancytopenia on hospital day 2, felt to be the result of IV hydration for his rhabdo, compounded by marrow suppression from acute EtOH and liver disease (causing known thrombocytopenia). We have ordered for repeat CBC to be scheduled two days after discharge. . 7. Insomnia/anxiety. We continued his outpatient Xanax and gave a small dose of Xanax at discharge for a taper over the ensuing three to four days. Patient understood that his primary provider in ___ would not agree to refill Xanax prescription (patient was contacted during the admission), and that the prescription we were providing was to ensure that he could taper the dose slowly so as to avoid withdrawal symptoms. . 8. Reflux symptoms. He was started on a PPI during this admission for reflux-type symptoms and empiric treatment of possible gastritis in setting of heavy EtOH. . He was kept on a normal diet. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ yo patient with history of migraines/cluster headaches, shingles recently treated, CAD, GERD, Anxiety, HTN, Hypothyroid, detrusor hyperreflexia admitted for evaluation of weakness and confusion . 1. Weakness and Confusion: Weakness was truly gait instability, patient had normal strength bilaterally. CT scan could not rule out NPH, however unlikely as patient's urinary symptoms were frequency, not incontinence, and is likely secondary to urinary tract infection, see below. Also, patient has a history of detrusor hyperactivity which can cause incontinence itself. Hallucinations/Confusion concurrent with benadryl administration, and change from baseline medications, imipramine discontinued and ___ added. Changed patient back to home regimen including imipramine and discontinued ___. Added haloperidol 0.25mg QHS to be taken PRN for confusion or agitation. Discussed possibility of discontinuing clonazepam and xanax with family and patient, however very resistant. In the future would consider discontinuing one and increasing the dose of the other. Avoided antihistamine agents. Patient's mental status was closer to baseline prior to discharge. Patient seen by ___, recommended rehab facility to continue to build strength. . 2. UTI: Most likely contributing factor to patient's confusion and weakness. UA positive. Urine cultures showed E. coli. Started on Ciprofloxacin 250mg BID on ___, with end date of ___. Patient had foley catheter placed in the ED, removed prior to discharge. . 3. Questionable EKG changes: ED reported ST changes in V4 and V5, however looked more like artifact as was only present in some beats. The patient never had any symptoms consistent with ACS, patient denied CP, SOB, diaphoresis, nausea. Two sets of cardiac enzymes were negative. Monitored patient on telemetry with no documentation of abnormal rhythms. . 4. HTN: Continued home regimen of imdur, metoprolol, and quinapril. Increased metoprolol to 75mg BID as blood pressure elevated. Monitored closely and adjusted as necessary. . 5. CAD: Continued above medications with enteric coated ASA and simvastatin. . 6. Shingles: S/p 5 days of valtrex administration. Continued neurontin for nerve pain. . 7. Insomnia/Anxiety: Continued clonazepam and xanax at home doses. Monitored very closely for signs of confusion and had very low threshold to discontinue. . 8. Hypothyroid: Continued levothyroxine. TSH elevated, however Free T 4 was normal. Increased levothyroxine dose to 75mcg once per day. . 9. Pre-diabetes: Maintained on ___ diet while inpatient. ___ BG showed mild elevations in high 100's up to 200. Patient most likely has diabetes. Continued to check ___ BG and will refer to primary care physician when to start treatment. Patient will likely need oral hypoglycemic. . 10. GERD: Switched nexium to pantoprazole while inpatient. Changed back to nexium when patient was discharged. . # FEN: Repleted fluids and electrolytes as needed. . # PPX: Heparin SC, PPI . # ACCESS: PIVs . # CODE: FULL CODE (confirmed with family) . # CONTACT: HCP ___, contact ___ ___ .

Physical therapy worked with you and will continue to work with you at the rehabilitation facility.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ YO F with HTN, AFIB s/p pacer complicated by post-cardiac injury syndrome presenting with chest pain, shortness of breath, and fevers c/w prior flares of post-cardiac injury syndrome after recent reduction in prednisone dosage. . # Chest Pain - The patient was admitted to the medicine service to rule out ongoing acute coronary syndrome. patient had three sets of negative cardiac enzymes and remained on telemetry for approximately 24 hours without event. Given negative ACS work-up and chest X-ray without signs of acute cardiopulmonary process, patient's other symptoms, and CRP > 300, the patient was felt to be having a flare of patient's known post-cardiac injury syndrome. After discussion with Dr. ___ outpatient ___, the patient's prednisone dosing was increased from 12.5 daily to 30mg daily. patient was encouraged to continue at this dose until otherwise instructed by patient's outpatient physicians. . # SOB - Slight congestion was seen on admission CXR c/w mild CHF although also has prior history of SOB with post cardiac injury syndrome exacerbations. patient did not seem to be in CHF on exam and was given lasix 60mg PO daily and spironolactone 25mg daily. (Patient reports taking lasix 60mg ___ per week and spironolactone 25mg daily at home.) BNP was also only slightly elevated at 2100. Given CXR, BNP, normal oxygen saturation, and constellation of symptoms, the patient's shortness of breath was felt most likely ___ post cardiac injury syndrome. . # Fever - The patient was febrile both in the ED and on the floor (to 103). patient was cultured on both occasions. Four blood cultures have not grown at >48 hours and a urine culture showed mixed flora c/w genital contamination. The patient was given tylenol for fever. Antibiosis was held. Given patient's recent history of eye biopsy, opthamology was consulted to rule out on-going eye infection or eye involvement of an auto-immune process. Opthalmology was able to reach one of the fellows involved in the patient's recent biopsy with preliminary results of the biopsy which was c/w a keratoconjunctivitis not associated with auto-immune or infectious phenomena. Rheumatology was also consulted for consideration of other auto-immune processes. They suggested "considering further imaging of cardiac area - ?PET CT?, ID and Heme/Onc evaluations as outpatient. If work-up is unrevealing, would consider temporal artery biopsy. Attempt to slowly decrease prednisone by 1 mg every ___ weeks." This information was relayed to the patient's PCP for continuity of care. The patient also had both rheumatology and pulmonary follow up appointments scheduled. . #. Hyperglycemia. Likely ___ prednisone although patient did not intially provide metformin as a regular home medication. It was unclear how regularly patient takes metformin but patient was encouraged to do so daily and was restarted while in the hospital. patient's FSBS ranged from the 150s to the low 300s. patient was additionally covered with sliding scale insulin. . # AFIB with pacer. The patient's INR was 1.3 at admission, felt likely ___ holding coumadin in the setting of eye biopsy. patient's coumadin was resumed at 5mg*2days then 7.5mg*2 days as per patient's home regimen. . # HTN. On ___ the patient was in good condition with stable vitals and was requesting discharge. The patient was discharged to home in good condition with a plan for follow up.

text: Brief Hospital Course: Patient Summary: ================= ___ with history of Meniere disease who presented to the ER with dizziness and word finding difficulty and was evaluated by neurology for stroke with CTA neck and brain that were negative. patient was discharged from the ED but returned for nausea/vomiting and headache and continued dizziness and gait instability. patient had an MR brain that showed a subacute/chronic bilateral cerebellar infarct. patient was admitted to medicine for management of n/v and headache. Tele without afib but we plan for outpatient cardiac monitoring to evaluate for paroxysmal afib. Echo with bubble study showed small PFO/ ASD. Will have outpatient Doppler of patient's lower extremities to rule out DVT. Vertigo and gait instability thought not to be related to old infarct as timeline of occurrence does not correlate with stroke. Headache was managed with multiple therapies including Sumitriptan with minimal effect. However, only Reglan was helpful in decreasing pain and nausea. patient received IVF for concern of viral gasteroenteritis with improvement of symptoms. Restarted on home HCTZ for Meniere's disease. summary: You came to the hospital because a mass was seen in the right atrium of your heart on a routine echocardiogram. You were placed on anticoagulation with lovenox and admitted for further imaging. You had an MRI of your brain to rule out metastatic disease and it was negative. You also had a CT of your chest which indicated that the mass in your heart is most likely a blood clot. There was no evidence of pulmonary embolism (blot clot to the lung). A cardiovascular surgeon was consulted and did not feel it was necessary to try to remove the clot right now and recommended continuing lovenox. You may need to have an MRI as an outpatient for further evaluation of the clot depending on the final read of your CT scan today. Someone will call you tomorrow to let you know if this will be necessary. We also are giving you a course of antibiotics to treat you for pneumonia because you have been having a persistent cough, your immune system is poor, and your CT scan looked like there could be a small infection. You will need to have another transesophageal echocardiogram in two weeks to look at the size of the clot and make sure it is shrinking. Someone will call you to schedule this.

text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ right handed yound patient with a history of seizures following head injury at age ___, who presents for recurrent seizures despite outpatient medication adjustments. Patient has both simple partial and complex partial seizures lasting one to two minutes but occuring mutliple times a month, with patient's last larger motor seizure in ___. We know that patient has left mesial temporal sclerosis by MRI, which has worsened over the past years. EEG testing here has not shown epileptiform discharges but in past showed slwoing with sharp waves over the left posterior quadrant. patient is now on three anticonvulsants without seizure relief. Plan is for LTM on EEG to try to capture and characterize events to assess whether patient is an epilepsy surgery candidate. Neuro: Patient placed on EEG for LTM. Initially, continued home doses of Lacosamide, Levetiracetam and Pregabalin. During admission, patient's seizure medications were weaned sequentially to attempt to capture and characterize seizures. patient had multiple events characterized by aura of anxiety and warming sensation followed by staring and behaviro arrest and then difficulty with speech. EEG captured these events and showed rhythmic sharp activity over the left temporal region. Patient restarted on home doses of Keppra and Pregabalin. Lamictal discontinued. New medication, Topamax, started in addition to home medications, which patient tolerated well. Transitional Issues: -Continue Keppra 1000mg po QAM and 1500mg po QPM -Continue Pregabalin 25mg po QAM and 150mg po QPM -Continue Topamax 50mg po BID -Meds to be titrated by outpatient Neurologist -Will discuss further testing needed for pre-surgical evaluation including PET as an outpatient

Stopped IV dilaudid given tolerating PO intake and could be given PO meds. We advanced patient's diet further and patient tolerated this without issue. Of note, on the prelim read, there was NO evidence of chronic pancreatitis on MRCP. Counseled patient's to avoid EtOH, avoid NSAIDs, and to use acid-suppressing medication (patient said patient has omeprazole at home) to help reduce chances of the pain returning and/or worsening. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ year old with CAD s/p PCI ___, repair of ASD, longstanding ETOH, PE <6mos ago, off his meds for past 4 days comes in with constant chest pain. . #. Chest pain: Patient continued to complain of ongoing chest pain that was not relieved by NTG when he came up to the floor. Chest pain resolved a few hours later. As soon as he felt better, he requested to leave AMA. PE was ruled out by CTA. Only two sets of cardiac enzymes were obtained. His first CK was elevated with normal MB and troponin, the second CK decreased to normal range, with negative MB and troponin in both sets. Only two EKGs were able to be obtained before patient left AMA. There were some small dynamic changes in the ___ EKG which showed new T wave inversion in leads V3-V4 and T wave flattening in leads V5-V6, changes compatible with ischemia. When patient requested to leave AMA, we repeated multiple times the importance of finishing up the workup, given his CAD history and EKG changes. Patient refused a EKG before he left, he threatened to pull out his peripheral IVs, and said he did not want the third set of cardiac enzymes. He stated that his mother was undergoing mastectomy that day, and he had to go see patient. He denied that the reason for leaving was that he wanted to drink alcohol. He was able to repeat to us that the risks of leaving early included "I could have a heart attack, and I could die". He also said if he has recurrent chest pain, he would seek medical care. After multiple failed attempts to persuade him to stay, he was discharged against medical advice. He refused scripts for his cardiac meds, including warfarin, saying he has medications at his mother's house. He did receive scripts for multivitamin, folate and thiamine. . #. Sinus tachycardia: The patient was initially tachycardic in the ED, likely due to the fact that he has been off his beta-blocker for 4 days and may be having beta-blocker withdrawal. Could also be due to anxiety or ETOH withdrawal. PE was ruled out by CTA. Metoprolol was restarted. Patient was given one liter of NS, and tachycardia improved. . #. Pulmonart Embolism: Patient was found to have subtherapeutic INR due to no coumadin for 4 days. Patient was given lovenox in ED. Coumadin was restarted. No more INR was obtained before patient left AMA. Patient was instructed to continue coumadin which he agreed. . #. ETOH abuse: Patient stated to night float that he might be interested in detox. He was also benzo tox positive, but not on prescribed benzos. Patient was put on CIWA scale, given multivitamin, folate and thiamine. Social Work consult was ordered but patient left AMA before being seen by Social Work. . # GERD: Omeprazole was continued. . # Hypertension: Metoprolol was continued. . # DVT Prophylaxis: Patient was found to have subtherapeutic INR due to no coumadin for 4 days. Patient was given lovenox in ED. Coumadin was restarted. No more INR was obtained before patient left AMA.

Since we did not finish the workup for your chest pain, we cannot say for sure whether it is related to your heart. However, you did get a CT scan of your chest which showed no clots in your lungs.

text: Brief Hospital Course: #New onset adventitious movements Patient presented with new history of choreaform-like movements in setting of missing Adderrall doses. Patient had been physiologically dependent on adderrall, taking both the long and short-term formulations for many years. Once patient was resumed on long acting adderall on the day following admission, patient's symptoms resolved. Overall these movements were thought to be secondary to medication-induced (i.e. Adderrall withdrawal) effects. #Recent Seizure Patient presented with a first time seizure one week prior to admission. The circumstances of this seizure were not clear, but it was in the context of significant stressors (going through separation from husband, restraining order was filed). In addition, patient had a noncontrast head Ct on admission which revealed findings consistent with a bleed from patient's known cavernoma. Either of these factors may have provoked patient's seizure. Patient underwent routine EEG for which preliminary reading was normal. Patient was started on Lamotrigine with plans for gradual uptitration as follows: Lamotrigine 25 daily, goal to titrate to 150 bid (25 daily for two weeks, then 25 bid for two weeks, then 50 bid for one week, and continue increasingy 25 bid in weekly intervals until at target dose). Given that patient had one isolated event and did not have any clear triggers for ongoing seizure, patient was considered low risk and not worthwhile to be started on topamax bridge while lamictal dose was being uptitrated. With regards to other possible AED choices, keppra was avoided given mood issues, CBZ and depakote were avoided given its possibility to lower threshold for choreaform movements. #Elevated Liver Function Tests Patient was found to have mild elevation in LFTs, particularly alkaline phosphatase elevation, mild AST/ALT elevation, normal bilirubin. patient did not have any abdominal pain and was afebrile and well appearing. Workup included right upper quadrant abdominal ultrasound which revealed hepatic steatosis. Patient did have elevated glucose levels and was diagnosed with diabetes, likely reflecting component of NASH. #Arthralgias Patient complained of bilateral hand and palm arthralgias, however no evidence of synovitis or rash. patient's exam did not reveal any abnormalities. patient initially was found to have a CRP of 15, raising some concern for rheuamtologic disorders, however this was of lower suspicion given no other signs of inflammation on exam and relviately unremarkable labs apart from elevated glucose and moderate LFT elevation. Initial autoimmune serologies were sent which were unremarkable. patient's symptoms were managed with NSAIDs and gabapentin. Moving forward, this can be uptitrated. #Diabetes Mellitus Glucose ranges high 100s to 200s during hospital stay. Was diagnosed as pre-diabetes prior to admission. Given A1c 9.8, likely new diagnosis of diabetes mellitus. - arranged for insulin 70/30 with ___ diabetes assistance. - continue insulin sliding scale - will need close PCP follow up upon discharge TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: -Continue Adderall 30mg XR daily. Defer additional short acting Adderall given that it could be exacerbating anxiety and likely contributed to adventitious movements on admission - Follow up with ___ management of diabetes. Patient was discharged with insulin 70/30, all insulin supplies and Metformin. - Follow up with PCP for management of hand pains and LFT elevation (likely hepatic steatosis) - Follow up with Neurology for monitoring response on Lamictal and addition medication titration. - Follow up with home Psychiatrist as previously scheduled

We also found that your blood sugar was high, which is why we started you on Insulin and Metformin for diabetes. We also started you on a medicine called Lamotrigine to treat your seizures.

summary: You were admitted to the general neurology service at the ___ ___ to investigate the cause of acute symptoms in your legs. Examination revealed weakness in your left leg, sensory changes in your right leg, and increased reflexes with "clonus" which all points towards a problem in the spinal cord. MRIs of the entire spine showed no abnormalities such as compression from vessel abnormalities or vertebral discs, obvious infection, evidence of inflammation, and clear lesions such as tumor. In addition, your brain MRI was normal. We also performed a lumbar puncture, which gave us a window into the fluid surrounding your brain and spinal cord. This showed no evidence of bleeding, inflammation or infection. It is possible the process reflects an early and or mild transverse myelitis (inflammation of the spinal cord) due to the recent flu shot. As discussed, please return immediately should you develop bowel or bladder dysfunction. Please return if the sensory changes expand to involve more of your body.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ yo w/ a hx of A-fib on coumadin, CVA, and hx of falls who presents w/ increasing confusion and failure to thrive at home. . #CONFUSION: The patient has a history of falls; however, there was no known fall since ___. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ yo F s/p Roux-en-Y gastric bypass ___, ampullary stenosis s/p choledochoduodenostomy ___ and three months of severe right-sided abdominal pain of unclear etiology who is admitted with worsening nausea/vomiting and inability to take po. . # GI: patient. ___ has had consistent abd pain over the past 3 months. This represents the fourth admission for patient's and this episode was reportedly distinct by the presence of nausea and vomiting. patient was kept NPO, given IV fluids, iv dilaudid PRN, and antiemetics for symptomatic treatment. MRCP was performed and revealed focal peripheral hyperenhancement with peripheral focal biliary ductal dilatation in segment VII (seen in past MRI) - mildly increased compared to prior. Interestingly, patient. ___ had no leukocytosis, fever, elevated LFTs, or increase in CRP/ESR to go with this diagnosis. Review of the MRI with radiology indicated that this segmental cholangitis with associated intrahepatic biliary dilatation was indeed real and enhanced (albeit mildly) compared to the past MRI. Furthermore, this correlated with the location of patient's pain. With close consultation with GI and Dr. ___ (outpt GI team), the decision was to treat the pt with augmentin for ___ weeks and assess how the pain would do on this regimen. Cipro was avoided for concern of interactions with patient's antidepressants (given h/o serotonin syndrome and past sensitivities to antidepressant medications). In addition, to help manage the pain, the pain service was consulted. The recommendation was to start Cymbalta at 60 mg daily to help manage the pain. However, because patient. ___ was already on Pristiq (a SNRI) and risk of Serotonin syndrome, the decision was to withhold treatment with this.By the end of the hospitalization patient was able to tolerate POs low fat diet and PO medications- but required 10 mg oxycodone every 4 hours for persistent abdominal pain. Prescription for oxycodone was given to the patient. The hope was that the antibiotics would help with the chronic pain. In addition, patient. ___ was treated with presumed SIBO - given the symptoms of diarrhea, bloating, and N/V s/p gastric bypass. patient was initially iv flagyl and then PO flagyl with good tolerance. Also prilosec was discontinued to help minimize the chances of redeveloping SIBO. patient. ___ also understands the importance of eventually reducing opiate use to help improve gut motiliy. The cause of the segmental cholangitis is not entirely clear. Gas (accompanying SIBO) and the reduced motility (that may accompany narcotics) can potentially lead to reflux of enteric material in the biliary limb of the Roux-en-Y, slightly increase pressure, and given the side-to-side choledochoduodenostomy, can also potentially increase the risk of cholangitis. However, this is usually associated with generalized (and not segmental) cholangitis. The MRCP showed some, mild pooling/stasis around the choledochoduodenostomy (b/w ampulla vater and anastomotic site) but the significance of this was unclear. The old op note also did not reveal the length of the biliary limb to see how plausible this enteric reflux is in contributing to the existence of the cholangitis. To rule out other etiologies of poor GI motility, TSH was checked (and returned normal), electrolytes were optimized, and meds with anticholinergic activities were generally avoided. Of note, nephrolithiasis was considered a possible etiology of patient's RUQ pain, but the MRCP on my read revealed no significant nephrolithiasis. U/A did not reveal hematuria. Given CaOxalate crystals, however, patient is at risk and this should be considered if pain were to recur or present with a different quality. #Diarrhea: intermittent loose stools --stool studies were sent but returned negative. Was attributed to SIBO. There was no further diarrhea during the hospitalization. #Anxiety: --given ativan 0.5mg iv x 1 --holding clonidine and diazepam as unable to tolerate po. Can be resumed. . . #PPX: --hsq was given initially, but eventually stopped when patient was able to ambulate. . FULL CODE HCP ___ (husband) # in OMR Letter sent to PCP ___ MD

The patient was counseled to avoid all products that contain acetaminophen until instructed otherwise by patient's doctor. When patient's liver recovers from the acute insult, patient will be able to take acetaminophen in moderation, never more than 2 grams per day. The patient was educated regarding other medications, including narcotics and over-the-counter medications that contan Tylenol. # Alcohol abuse: The patient drinks ___ drinks/day. patient has a history of alcoholism and is involved in alcoholics anonymous. RUQ ultrasound showed fatty infiltration of the liver, which suggestions that the patient may have some underlying liver damage from the alcohol. The patient was advised to stop drinking alcohol and attend AA meetings regularly. # Liver injury: The patient's liver injury was likely relatd to a combination of acetaminophen and alcohol toxicity, as explained above. Serologies for viral hepatitis were negative. # Orthostatic lightheadedness: The patient complained of orthostatic light-headedness. This is likely due to dehydration and oxycodone use. EKG did not show evidence of ischemia. Cardiac enzymes negative x 2. CTA chest negative for pulmonary embolus. No evidence of bleeding. summary: You came to the hospital complaining of episodes of hallucinations and also with lightheadedness with getting out of bed. You were found to have abnormal liver function tests. The cause of your abnormal liver function tests was likely cause by taking too much Tylenol (acetaminophen). Do not take any Tylenol, or any drug that includes the active ingredient in Tylenol (acetaminophen). Percocet and many over-the-counter medications contain acetaminophen. You should not take any of these medications. You hallucinations were likely cause by Chantix. Stop Chantix and talk to your primary care doctor about alternative strategies for smoking cessation. You had a liver ultrasound, which showed evidence of liver disease. This is likely due to alcohol. You should stop drinking alcohol, as it is damaging your liver. You had a CT scan of your chest, which did not show any evidence of blood clots. However, it did show some lung nodules that will need follow-up in ___ year with repeat CT scan to make sure you don't have a lung tumor. You should also quit smoking to decrease your risk of lung cancer. You were found to have gallstones but there was no evidence that this is the cause of your liver test abnormalities.
