text: Brief Hospital Course: ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: ___ yo patient with history of carotid artery disease, peripheral vascular disease, hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with chest pain concerning for unstable angina . # Unstable angina/CAD: Patient presented with exertional chest pain highly concerning for ACS. patient has strong family history as well as strong personal history of peripheral vascular disease combined with hypertension and dyslipidemia. No significant EKG changes on chest pain free EKG. TIMI risk score 4 without EKG changes or cardiac biomarkers. patient's story was very consistent with unstable angina therefore patient was loaded with plavix, continued on heparin gtt as patient was being ruled out for MI. patient then underwent cardiac catheterization which showed 3 vessel disease with 70% proximal LAD lesion and diffuse RCA stenosis. No intervention was performed at that time as it was unclear which was the culprit lesion. After the first procedure patient developed extreme tenderness to palpation over femoral access site however there was no evidence of hematoma. Femoral ultrasound did not show a pseudoaneurysm. patient subsequently underwent submaximal stress testing and developed ischemic symptoms during the test. Later that day patient was ambulating in the hallway when patient developed chest pain with deep ST depressions laterally and inferiorly on EKG tracing. patient was put on bedrest and restarted on heparin gtt while awaiting a revascularization procedure. Prior to revasculariazation, patient had several episodes of chest pain while at rest with EKG changes and was started on integrilin and nitro drips. patient went for cardiac catheterization and underwent successful stenting of LAD and rotational atherectomy with stenting of the ostial RCA. patient will need to continue ASA and clopidogrel for at least ___ year. . # Aortic stenosis: At time of presentation, history was also concerning for symptomatic aortic stenosis as patient has known history of AS. Physical examination revealed a soft systolic murmur and preserved S2 consistent with only mild disease. Echocardiogram was repeated which was consistent with this with only minimal aortic stenosis. . # Hypertension: Sub-optimally controlled on admission but likely a significant anxiety component to this as it trended down over short amount of time without intervention. patient's home regimen on admission included valsartan 160mg, atenolol 50mg daily and HCTZ. patient's blood pressure remained difficult to control with systolics consistently in the 140-150's with SBP as high as 200 during catheterization. patient was started on amlodipine and patient's valsartan was increased to 320mg. On this regimen patient's SBPs were mostly 110-130. patient was discharged with plans to record patient's BP at home and follow up with patient's PCP for further medication titration as needed. . # Mixed dyslipidemia: Patient with history of elevated LDL, low HDL and elevated triglycerides that has been difficult to treat. patient is currently followed in ___ clinic and is on regimen of zetia, tricor and crestor. Most recent lipid panel in ___ showed TC 126, LDL 64, HDL 28, ___ 171. Crestor was held and patient was continued on high dose atorvastatin while inpatient. Given that patient tolerated this without any myalgias, it was continued on discharge. patient's PCP ___ adjust patient's anti-lipid regimen as needed. . # History of breast cancer: Bilateral breast cancer s/p mastectomy, radiation and chemotherapy. Currently in remission. patient was continued on arimidex. . # Peripheral neuropathy: Related to chemotherapy. patient was continued on gabapentin without any issues. . # Restless leg syndrome: Well-controlled on current regimen therefore patient was continued on home dose of pramiprexole. . # Urinary Tract Infection: Patient complained of some burning with urination and had positive urinalysis therefore was started on ciprofloxacin, completing a 3 day course. Urine culture subsequently negative.

This is called a subarachnoid hemmorhage. It is very small and likely not causing you any disability. These bleeds are usually do to head trauma, but we have no history of you having any trauma. These bleeds are also associated with a condition called amyloid angiopathy, which results in a number of very small bleeds within the brain. It appears based on the MRI that you have this condition. This condition is also assoiciated with dementia of which you also seem to have. There is no particular treatment for this condition, we will just follow you in clinic. You also had a urine analysis that indicated that you may have a small urinary tract infection. We started you on a medication called Bactrim, but switched to an IV medication called ceftriaxone. We Your cultures were negative so there is no need for further antibiotics.

KUB did not reveal any evidence of obstruction. The GI service was consulted. On ___ patient's symptoms improved and an aggressive bowel regimen was undertaken including golytely x2L, miralax x2, dulcolax x2, colace, MOM without effect. Narcotics were discontinued. text: Brief Hospital Course: The patient was admitted to the medicine service with pancreatitis, thought to be gallstone-related. IV fluid hydration was continued, and patient was kept strictly NPO, with pain and nausea control with IV medications. # Pancreatitis The patient was initially kept strictly NPO with IV fluid resuscitation as above. However, after several days patient's pain improved slightly with medications, but it became clear that much of patient's pain was likely due to liver infiltration, and likely not from pancreatitis. patient's lipase was also noted to trend down significantly, and on PO challenge patient was able to eat and drink without nausea. . # Metastatic carcinoma MRCP was ordered to evaluate for presence of ductal gallstones and to further evaluate the hypoechoic liver lesions noted on abdominal ultrasound. However, despite pre-test axiolytics and pain control, the patient was unable to tolerate the MRI, and it was aborted before the test could be properly performed. The study was therefore nondiagnostic, but the limited images that were obtained showed innumerable lesions in the liver, as noted above. A CT torso was then performed to examine for evidence of metastatic disease. This showed, in addition to the liver masses, mediastinal, hilar, and right adrenal masses. . Following the CT findings, it was decided that a liver biopsy would be the best way to obtain tissue for biopsy, and an ultrasound-guided liver biopsy was performed on ___. The pathology findings were limited by the fact that the biopsy contained mostly benign tissue with only a small amount of abnormal tissue, but the report did show metastatic carcinoma with neuroendocrine differentiation of probable lung primary. . Following the biopsy findings, the oncology service was consulted. They felt that small cell lung cancer was the most likely diagnosis given the pathology and radiographic findings. They recommended consideration of outpatient chemotherapy after resolution of pancreatitis, and also MRI of head and spine to evaluate for presence of metastases, which might inform decisions regarding palliative treatment and/or prognosis. . Social work was also closely involved with this process, offering recommendations to the primary team regarding management of pain and anxiety, as well as helping the patient to understand implications of patient's diagnosis. . # Pain control: The patient came in on a steady narcotics regimen, taking 40 mg TID of Oxycontin for chronic back pain, with additional breakthrough Percocet. patient was initially given IV narcotics during the first few days of hospitalization, but when patient progressed to PO intake as above, patient was transitioned back to Oxycontin, requiring increasing regular doses. patient continued to report significant abdominal and back pain, though very much improved with increasing doses. At no point did patient become sedated on this regimen, though patient did report some constipation, which was treated with stool softeners. . # Anemia: There was no evidence of any active blood loss, and patient's anemia was thought to be likely chronic, stable during patient's hospitalization. . The patient was discharged to home with family and friends on ___, scheduled to follow up within ___ days with oncology and patient's PCP.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ year old patient with past medical history of GERD, cleared Hep C, Hep B, who presents with a week of mouth pain after revision of dental implants and swelling presumed due to oral cellulitis. 1) Ludwig's Angina/Intraoral Cellulitis: The patient was evaluated in the emergency department by ENT and Oral Surgery who thought no acute surgical emergency. patient never had symptoms of respiratory limitation or difficult with swallowing and ate throughout patient's illness. Imaging was without collection. Nevertheless, given degree of swelling, reported progression, and failure to improve on oral regimen patient was treated with meropenem and admitted to the ICU for monitoring. patient was converted from meropenem to ciprofloxacin/metronidazole/vancomycin and remained stable overnight without any hemodynamic instability or fevers. patient was called out the floor and converted to amoxicillin/clavulanic acid. Given history of questionable penicillin allergy (rash in adolescence) patient was observed for 24 hours on this medication with no signs of reaction. patient was discharged home to follow up with patient's periodontist andoral-maxillofacial surgery if desired. 2) Severe Pain/ Anxiety: Despite stable to improving findings on exam patient insistent of severe pain. patient acknowledged a great deal of pain and fear of pain and initially required oxycodone Q3hrs. After hospitalist explained that this would make it impossible for patient's to be discharged and after being told patient would need to use less patient was eventually weaned down to Q6hrs dosing without any indication pain had worsened. patient was started on standing acetaminophen as well as gabapentin given likely neuropathic component due to multiple procedures as well as for anxiolytic component. This seemed helpful and patient was discharged with a month supply of gabapentin and a two day supply of oxycodone. PCP had planned psych referral for anxiety and further discussing this was encouraged of the patient. 3) Allergic rhinitis: This was stable, patient was continued on patient's home fluticasone inhaler and loratidine. 4) GERD: patient was continued on patient's home omeprazole. 5) Presumed COPD: Pt uses albuterol QAM for wheezing at baseline but given long history of smoking seems likely this is due to COPD, in which anticholinergic ipratroprium would be preferred. This was started with good effect and patient was discharged with a prescription for this medication. 6) Smoking Cessation: patient expressed an interest in stopping smoking but was reluctant to use nicotine patches due to fear it would interfere with patient's implants. patient was encouraged to follow up with patient's PCP to discuss medications (i.e. buproprion) to help patient's quit. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES - patient will follow up with patient's periodontist to re-evaluate patient's mouth and assure things are healing. patient expressed a plan to follow up with another oral-maxillofacial surgeon and was given contact information for these services. -patient will follow up with patient's PCP to discuss further work up and treatment for COPD including likely referral to pulmonary clinic.

text: Brief Hospital Course: The patient is an ___ yoM w/ a h/o COPD on 2L O2 at home, AAA, who presented with somnolence per wife, some increased labored breathing and ECG with concerning T wave inversions. He was admitted for ___. He was evaluated by vascular surgery for a blue pulseless foot in the ED. . SOMNOLENCE: Per history with pt's wife, patient had to wake him frequently on the morning of admission. He may have been retaining CO2 due to worsening COPD exacerbation causing somnolence. By the time EMS arrived, it seemed his mental status had cleared. It is unlikely that this was neurologic event such as TIA or CVA and pt denies any new medications to cause this effect. He was monitored overnight and had no further episodes of somnolence or mental status changes. . SHORTNESS OF BREATH: The patient reported an episode the morning of admission during which his breathing was more labored and he felt short of breath. He states he has these episodes once a week. On the evening of ___, while in the hospital, he had an episode of tachypnea with a respiratory rate of 42. He stated that he felt anxious. At this time, treatment for COPD exacerbation was begun and the patient was put on Solumedrol 125mg IV q8 hours, Azithromycin 500mg PO qday and standing albuterol and ipratropium nebs. He improved after 1 hour. He reported being very anxious during this episode and states that when he is frustrated with things, he feels more short of breath. While attempting an ABG, he reported that the needlestick made him more short of breath. On ___ he was given 0.5mg PO Ativan for anxiety and stated that this made him feel better. He was discharged with Prednisone 50mg PO X 4 days (5 day total course) and Azithromycin 500mg PO qday X 1 day (3 day total course). He should continue his Flovent, Spiriva and Duoneb at home. . COPD: As described above, pt was treated for COPD exacerbation. It is recommended that he also be on a long-acting beta-agonist such as Advair. He can ___ with his PCP regarding adding this to his regimen. . ANXIETY: Anxiety played a significant component to his shortness of breath. His anxiety symptoms improved with 0.5mg PO Ativan. He was told to ___ with his PCP regarding further treatment of his anxiety with small doses of benzodiazepines which he tolerated well. . PULSELESS FOOT: In the ED, the patient was reported to have a blue, pulseless left foot while hanging it off the bed. He was immediately evaluated by the vascular surgery resident who found that the foot was hyperemic but had mostly resolved and had good pulses. On admission, pt had 2+ bilateral DP pulses. He reports that his foot often turns red (not blue) when it is low to the ground, and improves on leg elevation. Vascular surgery recommended an arterial study to evaluate his peripheral blood supply to the feet. After explaining this study as well as the risk of limb loss with peripheral vascular disease, the patient refused to have this done. Vascular surgery also recommended a CTA of the abdomen to assess his prior AAA. The patient also refused this study. The risks and benefits of these studies were explained to the patient and he was determined to have capacity to make this decision. It was recommended that he ___ with Dr. ___ of ___ Surgery in 2 weeks. The patient did not wish for us to make this appointment and Dr. ___ number was given to him on discharge. . T-WAVE CHANGES ON ECG: On comparison of old ECGs, no change was identified in ST segments or T waves. The patient had 2 sets of cardiac enzymes which were both negative. He denied symptoms of chest pain. This was felt not to be a cardiac event. . HYPERTENSION Pt was continued on Amlodipine 2.5mg PO qday. His blood pressure was well-controlled. . The patient was put on a regular diet, was given SC Heparin for DVT prophylaxis and Colace for a bowel regimen. He was DNR/DNI during this admission after a discussion with him. He stated he would not want resuscitation efforts or intubation. He stated he had "papers" at home for this. He should ___ with his PCP regarding his code status. He was discharged with PCP ___ on ___ ___. He was given prescriptions for Azithromycin and Prednisone. He was told to see Dr. ___ vascular surgery.

You should discuss this with your primary care doctor, ___ any medications to help with your anxiety. You were started on Prednisone and should take an additional 4 days of this medication, starting tomorrow. You should take 1 more dose of Azithromycin tomorrow. You should continue to take your inhalers and nebulizers as prescribed.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ year old patient with COPD on 3L home ___ s/p recent admission ___ for COPD exacerbation and newly diganosed LUL mass now admitted with respiratory distress. . #. Acute hypercarbic respiratory distress/Cough: On admission, the patient was complaining of 3 days of cough and SOB that acutely worsened overnight. patient presented to an OSH and was transferred to the ___ ED for further managment. patient was placed on BiPAP in the ED and transferred to the MICU. patient had hypercapneia with a PCO2 of 57 initially, and was placed on non rebreather mask with little improvement, and was then started on non invasive positive pressure ventilation. Patient however tolerated this poorly and required intubation for severe respiratory distress. During acute decompensation, It was noted that patient was taking very high frequency shallow breaths with a constant cough like sound generated in the upper airway. Patient was relatively easy to ventilate and this raised question of paradoxycal vocal cord dysfunction, phrenic nerve injury, etc. During intubation however, vocal cords were noted to be normal in appearance and during serial imaging diaphragms remained symmetrical. Patient was treated with pulse dose steroids and started on Azithromicyn. Given known left upper lobe nodule, a CT scan of the chest was performed and did not show any significant interval change. Patient was sucessfully extubated on ___ with short NIVPPV bridge. Patient was transfered to medical floor on ___. patient had an uneventful course and was discharged in stable condition. Pt has been having financial problems and has not been able to afford Tiotropium (Spiriva). Social work was consulted and patient was given Ipratropium instead. Patient was slowly weaned off steroids with taper over the next ___ weeks. #. Fibromyalgia: Difficult to control, with overt anxiety in spite of ___ medical regimen. We continued regimen with fentanyl patch, gabapentin, SOMA, darvocet, amitryptline and Propoxyphene #. Anxiety: Patient with many social stressors and difficult to control anxiety. Given progression of symptoms inspite of agressive therapy, patient was to follow up patient's outpatient psychiatrist to address patient's anxiety. # Anemia: During admission noted to be near baseline of 31. There was no overt bleeding or hemolysis.
summary: You came to the hospital with shortness of breath that is likely due to COPD exacerbation. As you were tiring out, we put you temporarily on a ventilator to help you breath. You recovered after one day and returned to your baseline functional status. We found on CT scan a lung nodule that needs to be followed up. Please see f/u appointments. You were discharged in stable condition.

text: Brief Hospital Course: A/P: ___ year old patient with history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, chronic pain, recent spinal stimulator implantation, h/o hip replacement, presented for ___ Cellulitis that has failed keflex and doxycycline # Cellulitis: Failed Doxycycline and Cephalexin as outpt after having been found to have cellulitis of the lower left leg during patient's last admission. Given recent surgery and artifical hips/stimulator, pt was started on Vanco 1gm IV q12h. On ___, cellulitis looked slightly worse, and extending b/l, with low grade temps of 99. As a result, pt was started on Unasyn for strep coverage. The following day after initiation of Unasyn 3gm IV q6h, the cellulitis improved, receeding erythema from the marking made on admission and the following day. Patient also reported feeling better, with decreased pain. These developments suggested possible streptococcus etiology, however, difficult to assess and could have still been MRSA/staph. patient was continued on IV antibiotics for one more day and eventually transitioned to PO antibiotics with Bactrim and Augmentin with plans to finish a ___t time of discharge, pt was afebrile (never with a recorded fever while admitted) and with stable VS. Blood cx from admission was pending at time of discharge with nothing growing. In addition, wound care consult was placed for venous stasis ulcers, could have been mode of entry. # Anxiety: Pt was started on ativan 0.5mg PO prn anxiety. A presciption for 10 pills was given to pt at time of discharge and the need for it should be reassessed by the outpt PCP. The patient also plans to follow up with an outpatient therapist for patient's significant anxiety and stress. # Hip/Back Pain: Occurred after near fall day prior to admission, resulting in back/hip pain. Pain did not improve after one day, and thus imaging was obtained which did not show any acute fracture. patient was seen by pain medicine who recommended continuing current drug regimen and to schedule f/up with the pain clinic in order to assess function of recently placed spinal stimulator. patient was intermittently given PRN extra doses of Oxycodone. # Chronic Pain: Continued home regimen. Spinal stimulator recently placed. # Hypereosinophilia: Recently admitted a week ago and found to have absolute eosinophils >1,800. Unclear if this is a baseline value for patient. Differential at time included neoplasms, adrenal insufficiency, allergic, vasculitides, and parasitic diseases. PCP was notified of this finding and was going to trend the CBC at patient's next visit. CBC/diff on admission showed a AEC of 550, borderline for absolute eosinophilia. It appears to be improving. It might be related to a medication patient was taking or given during patient's recent surgery prior to patient's previous admission. At this time, there is no evidence that the rash is an allergic reaction given that the rash was worsening while the AEC was normalizing. Also, the rash responded to antibiotics quickly. patient has good follow-up with patient's PCP and will be reassessed at patient's next visit. # S/p Spinal Stimulator: Low suspicion for infection at site, c/d/i. No elevation in WBC and afebrile during entire admission. # Hypothyroidism: Continued Levothyroxine. # HTN/CV: Continued Atenolol/Lasix. # HLD: Continued Simvastatin. Transitional Issues: -F/u Blood Cx -Assess cellulitis at next outpt visit -Wean pain medications as needed in the setting of recently placed spinal stimulator -Recheck CBC with diff to assess eosinophilia, currently downtrending

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ year old patient with history of bipolar disorder, HTN, and HL who presented from OSH with 1.5 weeks of vomiting and transferred for ERCP due to choledocholithiasis. #. Choledocholithiasis: patient was admitted afebrile, tolerating oral intake, and after OSH RUQ ultrasound showed choledocholithiasis. patient underwent ERCP on ___ without complication. A distal common bile duct stone was removed. A large 15mm stone was seen at the hilum which was partially fragmented and extracted but could not be fully extracted. A sphincterotomy was performed and a stent was placed in the left hepatic duct. patient will need repeat ERCP in 2 months for stent removal and to complete stone extraction. Cholecystectomy was recommended in the interval. patient's diet was advanced without complication and patient was discharged with 5 total days of ciprofloxacin. #. Hypertension: patient was continued on patient's home lisinopril. #. Hypothyroidism: patient was continued on patient's home synthroid. #. Bipolar Disorder: patient was continued on lamictal and carbamezapine on the doses that patient was taking per patient's primary care doctor. #. Anxiety: patient was continued on clonazepam and fluoxetine #. Prophylaxis: patient was given subcutaneous heparin for DVT prophylaxis #. Medication reconciliation: patient was not able to effectively communicate patient's full medication list and patient stated patient was on different medications than patient's PCP's medication list. Medications should be reviewed as an outpatient. #. Code Status: Full code
summary: You were admitted to the hospital due to stones in your gall bladder and the duct leading away from your gall bladder. You underwent a procedure called an ERCP and a large stone was removed from your common bile duct. You also underwent a stent placement and a sphincterotomy, which means that the muscle around your bile duct was cut and a stent was placed to allow stones to pass through more easily.

text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ y/o patient with PMH of hypothyroidism, obesity now s/p bypass causing anemia requiring IV iron, and h/o SVT in the past who presents with SOB and leg swelling likely secondary to anxiety. Left MICU AMA. # Dyspnea The patient presented with leg swelling, SOB and a history of recent travel and smoking. Concern was initially for PE. DDimer and LENIs were negative in the ED. Sturating well on RA with HR in the ___. TTE was suboptimal but did not show RV strain. Could not lie flat initially for CTA. CE cycled and were negative. Given high index of suspicion from history, the patient was started on heparin gtt and transferred to the MICU. In the MICU, the patient immediatly reported near complete resolution of patient's respiratory symptoms. patient was able to lie flat and a CTA was performed. Prelim read was no PE. A bedside US did not show evidence of pericarditis/effusion. The patient subsequently signed out AMA. Source of dyspnea is not completely clear at the time of discharge; echo, EKG, cardiac enzymes, and CTA have excluded the major immediately life-threatening causes. Anxiety, esophageal disorders, and other items remain in the differential. Symptoms had resolved by the time of discharge. # AMA: Patient reported that patient was feeling better and was expressing significant anxiety about not spending the night in patient's home. patient reported a past experience as the source of these strong emotions. It was explained to patient's that no definitive diagnosis of patient's dyspnea had been made at the time of patient's leaving AMA and that it would be in patient's best medical interest for patient's to stay in the hospital while the evaluation was continuing. patient was made aware of the risks of leaving the hospital without a formal diagnosis, including injuring, worsening symptoms, and possibly even death. The patient verbalized patient's understanding of these risks and appeared to have capacity to make independent decisions about patient's care. patient was therefore discharged against medical advice. # Anemia The patient has a h/o iron deficiency anemia. Hemoglobin on admission is 9.1 which is at or exceeds patient's baseline. No active issues. # Hypothyroidism H/o of hypothyroidism and on home levothyroxine which was continued. TSh sent and is pending.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ is a ___ transgendered patient with anxiety d/o asthma, headaches and healed L-corneal ulcer who presented with headache and left eye visual disturbance. # NEURO: He was seen by ophthalmology in the emergency room and was noted to have ___ vision in the left eye, ___ in the right. There was also a left inferior nasal field cut in the left eye. Neurological exam in the ED showed possible Left UE proprioceptive deficit without any other associated sensory/motor deficits. The monocular visual symptom localized anterior to the optic chiasm. Structures to consider were the eye/retina and the optic nerve. The normal Ophthalmology exam earlier effectively ruled out pathology involving the globe/retina, and the corneal ulceration is apparently a non-issue at this point, which left the optic nerve, which could be suffering compressive, ischemic, infectious, or inflammatory/demyelinating damage. Lyme and RPR were negative. CRP, ESR, B12 and folate were all normal. MR imaging showed no evidence of demyelination, no evidence of any pathology of the optic nerve. An MRI of the C-spine was also performed and was without any abnormality to explain the patient's intermittent proprioceptive deficits on exam. MRI brain did demonstrate an enlarged pituitary gland and so dedicated imaging of the pituitary was performed which demonstrated a mildly enlarged pituitary gland and prominent infundibulum indenting the optic chiasm. There were no obvious focal lesions in the pituitary gland. We felt that optic neuronitis was possible cause of his sx, and recommended that he have an LP done, which he declined to have done here. We recommend Visual Evoked Potentials be performed to evaluate this further. It is possible that the patient's symptoms are related to his pituitary enlargement, given the indention of the optic chiasm but the infundibulum. Migraine specturm is also a possibility, though the headache is not consistent with the patient's prior headaches and he has no prior history of visual disturbance with migraine. # ENDO: With regards to the enlarged pituitary gland, the patient reports that he recently switched his maintenance testosterone therapy from injectable to T-gel; it is possible that his hormonal supplementation the the cause of the enlargement. There are no clear signs of pituitary pathology other than enlargement on the MRI. Again, we did encourage an LP to evaluate for infection and inflammation, however the patient would prefer this to be done with the assistance of friends who were unavailable at the time of hospitalization. He will need repeat imaging of the pituitary in ___ months, depending on the results of visual fields and symptoms. # HEME/Rheum: The patient was noted to have an elevated PTT. ___ was positive at 1:40. Anticardiolipin antibody should be tested as an outpatient. TRANSTIONAL CARE ISSUES: He will need to follow up with neurology, opthalmology and his PCP. He was given all of these phone numbers on discharge.

text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ h/o migraines with aura, HTN, obesity, sedentary lifestyle, and anxiety p/w bilateral right sided visual field loss, concerning for an acute ischemic stroke. # Neuro: The time of onset of symptoms was not clear as patient thinks patient may have awoken with the symptoms at 0845 but first noticed the symptoms while working on a computer at ___. While patient had a mild head pressure sensation alongside this event, this headache was not similar to patient's prior migraines and this event had no preceding visual aura (prior typical wavy visual disturbance). Initially, thought it was most likely that patient had an embolic acute ischemic stroke although migraine variants of the elderly is also a possibility. MRI brain showed left occipital infarct. summary: You were admitted to the hospital with decreased vision in your right eye. An MRI of your brain showed that you had a stroke. We checked your labs for stroke risk factors and saw that your cholesterol was elevated, so we started you on atorvastatin to treat it. You also have a patent foramen ovale (a small connection between 2 chambers of your heart) so we were concerned that you may have had a blood clot in a vein which traveled through this connection to your brain. We checked you for venous blood clots and you DID NOT have any, which was reassuring. So, for a blood thinner, we started you on Aspirin daily. We would like you to have a number of blood tests checked for any abnormalities that could predispose you to strokes. A prescription is included. In terms of driving on discharge, we feel it is safe for you to drive. Your visual deficit is very minor so please continue to be aware of it and be careful to fully explore your right visual field when you are driving.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ year old patient with past medical history of dementia, diabetes type 2, hypertension, prior partial colectomy, ventral hernia, admitted ___ to ___ ___ with a syncopal episode, OSH course notable for severe encephalopathy, abdominal pain, concern for small bowel obstruction based on CT, episode of hypotension of unclear etiology, transaminitis attributed to shock liver following episode of hypotension, transferred to ___ for additional workup, now being treated for small bowel obstruction (resolved), PEs, aspiration pneumonia (resolved), and persistent encephalopathy. # MALNUTRITION/ASPIRATION RISK: Pt was unable to tolerate PO throughout much of hospital course. Tube feeds via Dobhoff have been started. Speech Pathology has evaluated pt and feels that difficulty swallowing is likely due to pt's mental status. PEG had been planned; however, family has since decided to hold off and continue Dobhoff for now in the hopes that swallowing function may improve if mental status improves, although this remains uncertain. Speech pathology felt it would be reasonable to trial nectar thickened liquids when patient fully awake and alert, but when attempted patient did not participate. Of note, ___ became clogged several times but was able to be cleared with warm water flushes. Recommend frequent warm water flushes to prevent this from occurring. # METABOLIC ENCEPHALOPATHY # DEMENTIA Neurology consulted during the admission. EEG negative for seizure activity. Neuro felt that patient's initial change in mentation was due to a toxic/metabolic encephalopathy rather than true seizure as initially thought. Brain MRI was obtained on ___, which was overall unrevealing except showed a FLAIR hyperintensity that was initially felt to be artifact, although was still present on repeat MRI on ___. The significance of this remains unclear, and the neurology team has recommended follow-up in their clinic n the upcoming months, likely with a repeat MRI. They also recommended checking a serum paraneoplastic panel to rule out an autoimmune encephalitis, although overall there was a low suspicion for encephalitis, particularly given the lack of progression on MRI and overall improving clinical picture. Should patient's clinical course worsen then patient should be evaluated more urgently. Patient currently on memantine, donepezil, and seroquel. patient's home clonazepam was stopped as it was felt this was contributing to patient's encephalopathy. Of note, the patient's son did not agree with stopping the clonazepam and was concerned patient is experiencing anxiety and panic attacks, but this was not evident to the medical team, and it was felt that patient's mental status was improved off the clonazepam. # ACUTE PULMONARY EMBOLISM: Patient ultimately placed on Rivaroxaban, day ___. C.diff negative x 2. Tube Feeds changed from Glucerna 1.2 to Jevity 1.2 with banana flakes ___ per discussion with nutrition. PRN loperamide started. Should tube clog, try warm water flushes to unclog - banana flakes had been started for tube feed associated diarrhea but were stopped due to concern dobhoff was not flushing well (possibly too small gauge for this); can consider uptitration of loperamide vs trial of restarting banana flakes carefully if diarrhea worsens - also concern during admission that dissolvable lansoprazole clogging dobhoff tube, so it was attempted to give this by mouth. text: Brief Hospital Course: Psychiatric: ___ patient with complicated medical history, recent prison history, and polysubstance abuse vs. dependence, with reported history of bipolar and anxiety, who presented to the ED apparently over-medicated and delirious, and stated that patient was depressed with thoughts of SI in the setting of being physically abused by patient's boyfriend. patient was then admitted to the unit. While here, patient initially reported still feeling depressed, with no suicidal plan or intent. Very quickly, the majority of patient's deliriogenic medications were reduced. patient was taken off Elavil (with no side effects, as patient had reported an OD on that in the past and could be quite dangerous for a person with significant impulsivity), patient was taken off Gabapentin (with no side effects), patient was stopped on Topomax (no known prescription, no side effects), patient's Klonopin was reduced to .5mg tid, patient's Percocet/Oxycodone (multiple prescriptions for unknown doses) was changed to 1tab q6h prn pain per orthopedics, and patient's Effexor was decreased to 150mg XR bid. With those changes, the patient's delirium resolved and patient presented in a euthymic mood, and was comfortable appearing Sleeping well, eating well and tending to patient's dialy needs. Additionally, while in the hospital, patient spoke with patient "spiritual mother" and grandmother, and decided to move out of ___, back to ___, which helped patient's mood improve. With patient's improved cognitive function, patient reported a decrease in patient's depressive symptoms, and although patient endorsed a low level of chronic suicidality, patient stated patient had no plans to act on it, citing patient's grandmother and the Church as protective sources. Additionally, patient found out that patient's boyfriend was being held in jail (without the ability to post bail), which additionally helped patient's to feel safe. patient had been feeling quite frightened by patient's boyfriend. patient remains in contact with the court advocate. Upon discharge, patient's medications were reconcilied as patient had been provided with a large number of various medications during recent Primary care appointment. Dangerous medications and contributors to patient's delirious state were removed and patient was provided with two weeks of Percocet 1 tab q6h, Klonopin .5mg tid, Seroquel 50mg bid, and Effexor XR 150mg bid. At time of discharge, the patietn no lomger presented as an acute risk to herself or others. Although this patient will always have some underlying risk of self-harm due to patient's history of ODing, substance dependence and impuslivity, these risks were reduced as much as possible during patient's admission. Additionally, as patient's plan is to go straight to ___, there is minimal risk patient will have any further interaction with patient's abusive ex-boyfriend and patient's grandmother was coordinated with during patient's hospitalization to confirm patient's train ticket and finances to allow patient's travel. Upon discharge, an appointment with a PCP was set up, and this person can make a referral to a psychiatrist. (patient was instructed to contact Medicaid to get a number right away in order to provide that to the new PCP). While patient was here, while taking 125mcg of Synthroid, patient was found to be slightly hyperthyroid by TSH, and patient's dose was changed back to 112mcg (which patient had been taking previously and had a stable thyroid on this dose. patient was given a persciption for 112mcg for two weeks upon discharge. patient was instructed to get patient's TSH retested when patient meets patient's new PCP. Regarding patient's delirium, patient's mental status resolved upon lowering the amount and dosing of deliriogenic medications. You also received treatment for pneumonia. Initially you were doing better and the chest tube was removed, then the fluid all came back and you had a more long-lasting chest tube placed. The palliative care team also came to meet you and assist with managing symptoms and nutrition. You unfortunately had to be on a restrictive diet due to the fluid in your lungs, but the nutrition team closely followed you and made some recommendations to rub oil into your skin. Later on in your hospitalization, you developed rectal bleeding from your cancer. You had a flexible sigmoidoscopy which showed that your known rectal mass was bleeding, and you had one session of radiation inpatient.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ yo F with asthma exacerbation, who presents with symptoms concerning for stroke, asthma exacerbation and elevated lactate. . . # Asthma/Reactive airways: The patient was treated with prednisone, nebulizers and cough suppressants, and patient's symptoms improved. patient was never hypoxic and patient's symptoms seemed chiefly related to cough, supporting more of an allergic/reactive airways etiology. CXR was not suggestive of an underlying infectious etiology. patient was discharged with a plan for a prednisone taper, and a recommendation to be seen in pulmonary clinic. . # Diabetes Mellitus: The patients oral hypoglycemic medications were initially held on admission. With prednisone administration, the patient had a significant increase in patient's glucose to the 400s. patient was then restarted on patient's home orals, and told to increase home lantus to 10, as well as increase patient's mealtime sliding scale. Patient was discharged with close PCP follow up to help patient's manage sugars during patient's prednisone taper. . # Anisicoria: Patient presented with a headache and reportedly nonreactive right pupil that was concerning for head bleed versus stroke. patient's symptoms had resolved on arrival to the ED; patient was seen by neurology who did not find any persistent neurologic deficits. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ yr patient with a PMH significant for DMII c/b ESRD, retinopathy, and neuropathy, HLD, CAD s/p ___ MIs requiring 2 stents, HTN, hyperparathyroidism presenting with worsening nausea, anorexia, malaise x ___ year admitted for initiation of HD. ## ESRD/HD: Patient was recommended for HD due to worsening symptoms such as nausea, anorexia, weight loss, metallic tastes, and confusion in the setting of Stage 5 CKD with a GFR = 10. These symptoms were significant disruptions in patient's life. In the month prior to admission, patient. ___ was no longer able to go grocery shopping, cook patient's meals or spend time with patient's grandchildren-- all activities that patient had previously enjoyed. On ___, day of admission, a tunneled HD catheter was placed in patient's right internal jugular vein without complications. Patient subsequently underwent 5 sessions of HD, which patient tolerated well. patient. ___ reported symptomatic improvement after HD such as increased energy and appetite. patient was able to take POs without nausea or vomiting. On ___ the patient reported that the metallic taste in patient's mouth had disappeared completely. By the day of discharge, patient reported that patient had returned to patient's healthy baseline and felt ready to resume patient's ADLs. patient was discharged in stable condition with symptomatic improvement. ## Cough: Patient reported a dry cough x6 weeks with associated 22# weight loss. These symptoms were concerning for TB because the patient immigrated from ___ and endorsed a history of a +PPD with unclear treatment course ___ years ago. Therefore the patient was placed on respiratory precautions and a rule out TB protocol was initiated. Three sputum samples were collected from the patient, and all three on preliminary read were negative. A chest CT showed no evidence of active TB infection but extensive evidence of remote TB infection. Throughout patient's hospital course, the patient remained afebrile without a leukocytosis. On discharge it was recommended that patient follow-up with patient's PCP to start INH therapy to treat latent TB and prevent reactivation. ## Subclinical hyperthyroidism: patient. ___ presented with a low TSH with normal free T4 and T3. The patient denied symptoms of hyperthyroidism such as heat sensitivity, increased frequency of bowel movements,tremor, palpitations, anxiety. On exam patient did not have any signs such as stare, lid lag or skin changes. Given that the patient was asymptomatic and euthyroid, no acute intervention was necessary. The patient was recommended to follow-up with an endocrinologist on discharge. ## Enlarged thyroid goiter: On exam patient had an enlarged thyroid extending to patient's left chest. This was correlated with findings on chest x-ray (for evaluation of TB) and chest CT, which was reported as "a left paramediastinal mass was identified adjacent to the left apex." On thyroid ultrasound, it was further characterized as "a markedly enlarged left lobe of the thyroid gland with multiple confluent nodules." While the patient had been previously worked up for thyroid nodules, they are concerning because of their increase in size from ___. Patient was recommended to undergo further evaluation as an outpatient with a FNA. patient will need to discuss referral with patient's PCP. The endocrinologist who patient saw in ___ was contacted and stated that he was no longer following patient's as patient's PCP had been following patient's thyroid function. ## Anemia of chronic disease: Patient has a normocytic anemia with a high ferritin and normal Fe, B12 and folate consistent with anemia of chronic disease. Patient was treated with ferrous sulfate supplements and epogen at HD. Throughout this hospital stay, the patient did not experience any bleeding or other complications of anemia. ## Nutrition: Patient reported 22# weight loss in the precious 3 months. Albumin however was normal, which was reassuring. During this hospital stay, patient reported good appetite and ability to take POs. patient was also started on nephrocaps to supplement patient's diet. patient's vitamin D was also stopped as the renal dialysis team no longer felt they were necessary. ## Hepatitis B: Patient is not immune to hepatitis B and would benefit from immunization at an outpatient. ## Hypertension: Stable. Our target BP was 130/80 given that patient is DMII. We continued the patient on patient's home medications metoprolol and amlodipine. HCTZ was stopped due to low efficacy in the setting of a low GFR. ## DM-II: Stable. Patient was placed on an insulin sliding scale with fingersticks with meals. patient's glipizide was decreased from 10 to 5 mg due to concerns of hypoglycemia. ## CAD s/p ___ MIs and 2 stents: Stable. Patient reported no symptoms of chest pain or pressure. A baseline EKG was done which showed evidence of an old inferior MI. ## HLD: Stable on avapro and vytorin. ## Hyperparathyroidism: Elevated PTH likely secondary to CKD. At this time, the patient is asymptomatic with normal Ca and Phos and therefore no further invention is needed. Transitional Issues Upon Discharge Patient was discharged with symptomatic improvement of patient's ESRD after 5 sessions of HD without complication an completion of the rule-out TB protocol. As an outpatient, patient should follow-up with patient's PCP in regards to INH treatment for latent TB. The final results of patient's sputum smears and cultures should also be followed-up. Furthermore patient should receive the HBV vaccine series with patient's PCP. Patient will also need to follow-up with patient's endocrinologists for further work-up and management of patient's subclinical hyperthryoidism and multinodular goiter. It is recommended that patient have an FNA to rule out malignancy. Lastly patient will receive HD as an outpatient basis with plans to transition to PD. patient should follow-up with patient's nephrologist.

FSBS normal during episodes, atrial tachycardia on telemetry (unchanged, HR 110s consistently), neuro exam nonfocal. CT head was negative. Multiple episodes captured on video EEG which showed no abnormalities. MRI/MRA showed chronic small vessel ischemic disease, no acute infarcts. Final diagnosis most likely pseudoseizure in the setting of stress at home (husband sick, patient was recently sick, worried about who will care for patient's at home). patient was started on fluoxetine 20mg daily for mood and anxiety. Infectious workup also negative. We explained to patient and the family (daughter and son) that these episodes are stress related and not dangerous. If patient experiences onset, patient should sit down to prevent from falling. Family continues to be concerned about these episodes but understand that we have ruled out cardiac and neurological causes and these are benign episodes. Nausea, vomiting and lightheadedness are all listed as common side effects of bromocriptine. patient may also have some component of vertigo, which patient reports having had daily for a couple of months. History of HTN: There is documentation of HTN in patient's chart from the OSH, however patient is only on beta blockers, and patient has been normotensive throughout patient's hospitalization with one episode of hypotension. text: Brief Hospital Course: patient ___ is a ___ patient with history of mitral valve prolapse and palpitations, visiting ___ from ___, who presented to the ED with on going chest pain from 11pm the evening prior to admission. patient described patient's pain to the left anterior chest with occasional radiation to the left arm. Of note, about 6 weeks ago patient was admitted to another hospital for work-up of palpitations which was reportedly negative including what patient called a "PE study" and an echocardiogram. Below is patient's brief hospital course. # SCAD On arrival to the ED, patient's EKG showed ST elevations in lead II, III, aVF with positive troponins (0.33-->0.96-->1.93-->1.03) consistent with STEMI. patient was taken urgently to the cath lab which showed 100% stenosis in the distal LAD with sudden vessel taper and occlusion consistent with a spontaneous coronary artery dissection. No intervention was performed. patient was transferred to the CCU and started on metoprolol succinate 12.5mg daily along with aspirin and clopidogrel 75mg daily. In the CCU, patient remained free of chest pain and vitally stable. patient's heart rate and blood pressure at this time does not permit further up-titration of medications. TTE obtained showed EF 52%, normal left ventricular cavity size with mild regional systolic dysfunction most consistent with single vessel coronary artery disease (distal LAD distribution). Mild mitral regurgitation with normal valve morphology. # Fibromuscular dysplasia A screening CTA of the head and torso was performed. The CTA head did not show any evidence of aneurysm or vascular malformation. The CTA torso showed fibromuscular dyplasia of the bilateral renal arteries. patient is recommended to have appropriate follow up with a vascular medicine specialist which was discussed with patient's in detail prior to discharge. #Anxiety: Continued home Xanax 0.5mg PRN BID for anxiety. #CODE: Full code ___ Relationship: HUSB Phone: ___ TRANSITIONAL ISSUES =================== [ ] Consider cardiac rehab [ ] Consider ace-inhibitor for FMD if blood pressures can tolerate [ ] Consider initiation of SSRI for anxiety

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ year old patient with a history of HTN and pulmonary HTN who presents with SOB and hypoxia. . # Hypoxia, SOB: CHF versus pneumonia were on differentials. Pneumonia was considered with pt's history of progressively worsening cough and shortness of breath with leukocytosis and subjective fevers. On hospital Day 2, pt was febrile to ___ and was started on Levaquin. CXR shows pleural effusions but no lobar consolidations, and given that pt recently stopped diuretics, it was likely pt was fluid overloaded. This was supported by pt's elevated BNP. TTE showed moderate mitral regurgitation and pulmonary hyptertension (stable from prior). Pt was diuresed with Lasix and given captopril for BP control but was discontinued after UOP decreased and creatinine increased. Pt did well with antibiotic and patient's oxygen supplementation was weaned. patient was discharged on levofloxacin to complete a 7-day course, as well as furosemide 10mg daily until patient sees patient's PCP ___ ___. . # HTN: Pt was on felodipine, atenolol and Losartan as an outpatient. Pt came in with SBP in 190s and we continued felodipine and started TID captopril. On hospital day 2 pt became oliguric and Cr bump to 1.3 and thus stopped captopril. SBP in 130s and we restarted home atenolol. Once ___ resolved, all home antihypertensive medications were resumed, as well as furosemide as noted above. . # Anxiety: Pt was having multiple anxiety episodes upon admission and we continued patient's home diazepam. During these episodes, pt's BP increased significantly with tachycardia and had periods of nausea. Pt received valium at night and an ativan when patient was particularly anxious. # Hyponatremia: Pt's sodium remained low throughout MICU course and has a history of having diuretics changed due to hyponatremia. Urine lytes, osm and urea were checked which showed low Na and osm consistent with dehyradation. Pt was hydrated and hypoNa resolved. # Anemia: Pt has h/o of anemia which had been worked up recently with EGD and colonoscopy. Would recommend outpatient follow-up given that patient's Fe was 7 and TIBC was low during admission. . # Hypothyroidism: Chronic and stable. We continued Synthroid at home dose. . # Renal lesions: Two renal lesions were seen incidentally on CT. Recommend that PCP get renal ultrasound to further characterize and to eval for renal cell carcinoma (considering patient's iron deficiency anemia of unclear etiology). . # Transitional Issues: - Needs renal ultrasound - Anemia workup

CT head reassuring. Serum and urine tox screens were negative. TSH mildly elevated at 5.9 but unlikely the cause of patient's symptoms. Of note was recently started on baclofen as an outpatient (___) which was discontinued as this could have been contributing factor, though patient only received one dose prior to admission. During admission impression was that patient has parkinsonian "off" phenomenon in the early AM hours prior to getting patient's meds, but subsequently AAOx3, interactive and entirely appropriate during the day AFTER patient gets patient ___ medications. At discharge patient is back to patient's preadmission baseline and discharged home with home health aid and plan for close PCP and neurology follow up. # CT EVIDENCE OF ASCENDING COLITIS CT A/P demonstrated proximal ascending colonic fat stranding concerning for infection vs. inflammation vs. ischemic injury. No evidence of perforation, lactate on admission normalized. CRP normal. Colonoscopy ___ notable for rectal prolapse, large external hemorrhoids, melanosis, a few distal diverticula. No acute evidence of infection. Brief course of empiric antibiotics was discontinued given clinical stability. Can consider outpatient colonoscopy for further work up pending discussion with PCP. # ASPIRATION RISK Due to ___ mental status on admission c/f swallowing ability. S&S evaluated patient after mental status improved and recommended diet of pureed solids/thick liquids. They stated that video swallow could be pursued to further characterize aspiration risk. Clinical history of coughing after eating is concerning for aspiration. Discussed ongoing risk of aspiration with son/patient and decision was made to continue oral diet. No current interest in tube feeds. Patient should continue aspiration precautions (discussed below) # ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY Cr elevated to 1.2 on admission from baseline 0.6-0.9. Trazodone, mirtazapine, and tramadol were discontinued given concern for Serotonin syndrome. Seroquel and Sinemet were kept at the family medication list dosages, NOT the dosages from the ___ list. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ is a ___ patient with systemic diffuse large B cell lymphoma with CNS involvement who presents with worsening CNS disease and CNS hemorrhage. ACTIVE ISSUES: ============ 1. Cerebellar Hemorrhage: Prior to admission patient developed an occipital pressure headache, accompanied by nausea but no vomiting. Head CT and MRI showed dural blood in both of the inferior portion of the cerebellar hemispheres. The differential diagnosis includes (i) new dural CNS lymphoma in the cerebellum or (ii) plain hemorrhage because patient was also concurrently anticoagulated for patient's atrial fibrillation. Patient received 10mg of dexamethasone and then Dexamethasone 4 mg daily, tapered to 2mg daily upon d/c. Started on Keppra for seizure prophylaxis. Lovenox stopped. Cycle 1 Rituxan and cycle 4 HD MTX chemotherapy administered and well-tolerated (see below #metastatic lymphoma to brain). Neuro exam stable on discharge without cerebellar signs. 2. Metastatic Lymphoma to the Brain: Cycle 1 Rituxan and cycle 4 HD-MTX chemotherapy administered and well-tolerated. Urine alkalinization with sodium bicarb 150meq/L IVF + sodium bicarbonate 1300mg PO q6hr to maintain urine pH >8.0 to enhance MTX excretion. Leucovorin rescue starting 24 hours after MTX. MTX level at 72 hours was 0.11. LP was performed this admission and CSF cytology suspicious for malignant cells. 3. Gait Instability: Likely from CNS disease and cerebellar hemorrhage. Physical therapy worked with patient and felt that pt would benefit from rehab upon d/c, however pt declined and agreed to staying at son's house with home physical therapy. 4. Atrial Fibrillation: Patient was on lovenox at home, but given risk of fall and CNS hemorrhage, lovenox was discontinued. Started aspirin 325, as CHADS2 score is 2 (age, HTN). 5. Hypertension: Goal SBP < 180 given stroke risk. Pts SBP were 170s, HR is in mid-40s to ___. Adjusted pt's home BP meds for improved BP control without decrease in HR. Decreased metoprolol succinate from 50mg to 25mg daily. Increased valsartan from 20mg BID to 80mg daily. CHRONIC ISSUES: ============= 1. CAD: Continued metoprolol, valsartan, furosemide (see above #HTN). 2. Hyperlipidemia: Held statin during hospitalzation ___ interaction with MTX. Restarted on discharge. 3. Hypothyroidism: Continued home levothyroxine. 4. Left L3 radiculopathy: This is not an issue at this time, no interventions. 5. Anxiety: Ativan HS:PRN for sleep TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: =============== - Return during the week of ___ for rituximab and HD-MTX chemotherapy. - Consider amantadine in future for fatigue sx.
summary: You came to the hospital with headache, neck pain, and nausea. We found that you had some bleeding at the back of your brain due to your cancer. You were treated with Rituxan and methotrexate chemotherapy and steroids (dexamethasone). You were also started on an anti-seizure medication to prevent any possible seizure. Fortunately your headache resolved. Given the bleeding, you should stop Lovenox, which can put you at risk for future bleeding.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ w/ Alzheimer's dementia, celiac sprue, HLD, anxiety, GERD presents from patient's facility with increasing somnolence and WBC 19 in the setting of stage IV pressure ulcers and possible osteomyelitis. patient's mental status has improved to baseline dementia and patient is being discharged back to ___, patient's assisted living facility. --------------- ACTIVE ISSUES --------------- # SOMNOLENCE: On presentation, the patient was very difficult to arouse, even to sternal rub. Etiology of patient's somnolence is not entirely clear but most likely related to ongoing infection, given patient's leukocytosis, with contribution from progressive dementia and possibly also from constipation. The most likely source of infection is osteomyelitis secondary to patient's two stage IV decubitus ulcers (over patient's coccyx and right hip). patient's mental status improved to baseline during patient's hospitalization after several interventions, including Vancomycin & ceftriaxone, IV fluids, relief of constipation via manual disimpaction, and discontinuation of patient's home olanzapine. Therefore, it is not clear what the primary cause of patient's somnolence was. However, patient was discharged at baseline mental status; alert, oriented only to self and responsive to name, interactive but not following commands consistently. # OSTEOMYELITIS and PRESSURE ULCERS at right hip and coccyx: These ulcers per report were present for the past several months. Currently both are stage IV, suggesting a presumptive diagnosis of osteomyelitis. After discussion with the Infectious Disease team, it was felt that patient's osteomyelitis was likely not the cause of patient's acute mental status change. patient's family did not want aggressive intervention, including debridement or bone biopsy. The Infectious Disease team felt that without debridement, antibiotics alone would be suppressive not curative and may ultimately lead to resistance; however, it may be a good temporizing measure depending on family preference. Ultimately, appropriate wound care of the pressure ulcers is most important. The patient was discharged on Augmentin 500mg TID for suppressive therapy for osteomyelitis, with the understanding that if patient experienced too many side effects, this medication can be stopped in the future. Additionally, Wound Care nursing recommended: reposition patient Q2H and prn, using pressure cushion and mattress, clean ulcer with wound cleanser set, fill wound with aquacel followed by dry gauze and softsorb/ABD, change daily. Nutrition recommended: Ensure Plus TID, multivitamin with minerals, and vitamin C supplementation. # LEUKOCYTOSIS: ___ improved from 19 on admission to 12.9 on ___ with Vanc/ceftriaxone. Etiology of leukocytosis is unclear etiology, but stage IV pressure ulcers with underlying osteomyelitis are most likely infectious source. Urine culture negative, blood cultures NGTD, CXR negative, lung exam clear, and stool C diff test is negative. Per my discussion with the family and Infectious Disease, as detailed above, the patient will be discharged on Augmentin 500mg TID for an indefinite course for suppression of osteomyelitis. Trop and BNP as well as stable EKG make cardiac cause very unlikely. Absence of hypoxia demotes PE. Abx were held after dose of levofloxacin in the ED since chronic symptoms, no evidence of recent decompensation, and do symptoms except dyspnea (no cough, no hypoxia). The pruritis returned two days after the third dialysis session, but again resolved after patient's next HD session. patient was continued on patient's home Sevelamer dose. Hydralazine was discontinued for more blood pressure room. Potassium supplementation was discontinued. patient was scheduled to have fistula creation during patient's stay but this was postponed to the near future as an outpatient. # Hypoxemia: Sats on admission were at recent baseline of 91-93% on RA while at rest. patient's sats began to decline during the first week of patient's hospital stay. This should be titrated up as needed. # UTI: At ___ patient was started on ciprofloxacin for treatment of UTI. Due to concer for decreased seizure threshold, we changed the cipro to ceftriaxone. ___ had not sent a urine culture so we sent blood and urine cultures while patient was here. patient's urine culture ended up growing pan-sensitive enteroccus. Due to concern for aspiration (see below) we switched the antibiotics to zosyn and vancomycin. Upon respiratory improvement, we switched patient's antibiotics to augmentin to complete a ___ day course. # Pneumonia: patient developed an O2 requirement during patient's admission.
